# General shadow update cadence feasibility

2026-10-06. Read-only pinned Iris/Photon assessment. **Reject a whole-map cadence
implementation as the next current-scene performance experiment.** A snapped
projection cell and unchanged light do not certify unchanged shadow content;
simple draw cancellation is invalid; current cost evidence is weak and the
roughly 60 FPS coastal workload would produce roughly 30 Hz shadows if blindly
updated every other frame. This is a priority decision, not proof that temporal
shadow approximation is universally impossible or perceptually unacceptable.

This question substantially overlaps the retained
[temporal cache design](PHOTON_SHADOW_CACHE_DESIGN.md). The new audit rechecks its
transaction against current pinned binaries and applies current performance
evidence. It does not revive the rejected extra-pass classifier/cache work or
implement another framework. Root owns all builds, clients and GPU work.

## Source authority and exact checks

Iris NeoForge 1.8.12+mc1.21.1 SHA-256
`3e3f94d2d5cdcb8145c4385d521974aa2d8669b2cc212351f70cf06488182e83`;
Photon v1.3b SHA-256
`120897768eaa8cb1f14a3e98f88dff009ae3204ee3b96904a4fe8586edfc1ead`.
Photon is by Benjamin Stott (SixthSurge); source/license unchanged.

Ignored evidence: `build/shadow-cadence-feasibility-r1/`. JDK 21 `javap -p -c`
actually ran against ShadowRenderer, ShadowMatrices, ShadowRenderTargets,
MatrixUniforms and IrisRenderingPipeline. Eight selected Photon files were
extracted read-only; `provenance.json` records exact hashes. `result.json` passes
15 bounded source checks and retains the historical timing inputs, hypothetical
screen arithmetic and limitations. No tests, Gradle task, source patch, client,
reload or GPU measurement ran. No owned live processes remain.

## What reuse would actually have to preserve

`IrisRenderingPipeline.beginLevelRendering` clears shadow depth at offset 281,
dispatches shadow compute programs and executes shadow color clears, before
the frame notifier at offset 449. A decision in the new CoreUniformFrame
listener is already too late to prevent these clears. Cancelling only
ShadowRenderer.renderShadows would retain cleared targets, not a cached map.
Full-clear requests must refresh. Unrelated custom-image clears and frame
updates must continue; cancelling the entire begin method is invalid.

The original ShadowRenderer transaction changes ACTIVE, render buffers, viewport,
projection and culling state, prepares terrain, draws opaque/cutout casters and
entities/block entities, copies opaque-only depth, draws translucent terrain,
generates mipmaps, restores state and runs shadow composites. Reuse must occur
before mutation and retain a coherent set of shadowtex0, shadowtex1, color outputs,
mipmaps and actual target/flip identities. Unknown image/compute/composite effects
must fall back to rendering. Photon COLORED_LIGHTS writes a voxel image from
shadow vertices; cached depth cannot replace that work. Water caustics can change
shadowcolor while caster depth stays identical.

Holding ShadowRenderer.MODELVIEW/PROJECTION alone is insufficient. Iris
MatrixUniforms registers independent PER_FRAME sampling suppliers that recreate
the model-view from camera/light inputs, plus its inverse. Map projection,
model-view, inverses and the map's camera origin must be captured and supplied
together. For current camera-relative position p, the retained map requires:

```text
clip = P_cached * M_cached * (p + C_current - C_cached)
```

Photon's nonlinear shadow distortion follows that transform unchanged. A camera
turn can expose receivers/casters missing from the old culled map even if the
coordinate mapping is correct; grid-cell equality does not prove frustum
coverage. Signed float remainder is used by ShadowMatrices snapping, including
negative coordinates. Projection near/far may depend on DH distance. Reload,
resize, dimension, map layout, shadow radius and projection changes invalidate
the complete transaction. Source `dhShadow.enabled=false` is not DH compatibility
acceptance for another directive or pack.

## Why a cell/light key cannot certify reuse

Photon shadow.vsh calls animate_vertex for terrain. Its displacement uses
frameTimeCounter for wind, rainStrength/weather wind, and eyePosition for plants
pushed by the player. These may change geometry without a chunk rebuild or
camera snap change. Shadow.fsh uses caster texture alpha/color at LOD 0; resource
pack animation can change coverage/transmission with fixed meshes. Entities and
block entities use partial-tick animated poses; player shadows remain enabled
independently of the general entity option. Block edits, chunk uploads, new
visible casters, resource reloads and third-party renderer callbacks also need
real producer epochs. Entity counts/positions or elapsed warmup are inadequate.

The older audit's assumption that sun angle continuously interpolates was
corrected in [the visibility design](SHADOW_VISIBILITY_CACHE_DESIGN.md): exact
Minecraft 1.21.1 time-of-day ignores the partial-tick parameter and uses stored
dayTime. Light may therefore stay unchanged between normal ticks. That creates
an opportunity for transform equality, not equality of animated shadow content.

A whole reused map delays nearby moving-player/foliage/entity shadows together
with distant shadows. It cannot keep near dynamic shadows current while caching
only far/static ones. Redrawing dynamic casters over retained depth leaves old
silhouettes when they move; clearing removes the retained base. A static/dynamic
split needs separately proven storage/merge or partial-region coverage machinery,
which is outside this no-new-target bounded assignment. Fixed camera/time saves
with animation disabled would prove a changed static workload only. They cannot
establish general gameplay benefit and are rejected as product evidence.

Shadow visibility traversal caching is a separate exact CPU concept. Its
[existing design](SHADOW_VISIBILITY_CACHE_DESIGN.md) preserves touched-section
stamps, graph directions, task queues and list generations; retaining a geometry
list alone is insufficient. It does not establish texture reuse, is not enabled,
and should not be confused with the rejected extra-pass shader cache.

## Cost evidence and screening ceiling

Current pixel/atlas/water cost controls export whole-frame GPU intervals only.
**The current complete shadow refresh transaction cost is unknown.** Atlas's
3.44% first contrast and large control drift do not identify shadow-map cost.
Receiver filtering remains every frame even when generation is reused; shadow
PCF/SSRT/volumetric reads cannot be counted as generation savings.

Historical original-Photon attribution summaries and selected raw records were
inspected; their paths and hashes are retained in result.json:

| Historical scene | GPU shadow mean, ms | CPU shadow wall/thread mean, ms | GPU rows / zero fraction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Forest | 0.394292 | 1.587967 / 1.584171 | 120 / 9.17% |
| Coast | 0.529033 | 1.116171 / 1.112083 | 68 / 35.29% |

These are interleaved N5/seven-category GPU command intervals, not an additive
one-frame decomposition. Tiny/zero timer values have the existing Apple-driver
precision limits. CPU shadow scope contains its child terrain work; those cannot
be added. The interval excludes shadow clears occurring in beginLevelRendering.
Detailed instrumentation changes the workload. Neither historic number bounds
the current complete transaction, proves CPU/GPU critical-path overlap, or
predicts gameplay savings. Both raw reports have the shadow eligibility observer
disabled, with zero completed observation frames; no runtime hit rate follows.

The useful mathematical screen is saving <= r * S before guard/refresh overhead,
where S is the measured removable refresh transaction on the actual critical path
and r is the eligible skipped-frame fraction, at most 0.5 for alternate-frame
cadence. S is currently unknown. A **hypothetical** half of the historical GPU
interval is only 0.197146/0.264517 ms; it is a scale warning, not a hard ceiling.

Using the earlier actual pixel screen solely as a planning denominator
(native-before 16.5924 ms, live .75 15.2448 ms), reaching 1.20x original FPS would
need another 1.4178 ms off live frame duration. With r=0.5 and ideal linear
critical-path savings, S would have to exceed about 2.8356 ms. A 5% incremental
FPS screen would need S about 1.4519 ms. Guard cost, forced refreshes and overlap
increase those requirements. These assumptions are not measurements; combining
candidate percentages is not justified. Current history derivative is unmeasured.

## Conditional future hypothesis and stopping decision

Temporal cadence remains a possible **approximate** general work budget for a
different high-FPS, demonstrably shadow-bound workload. The retained design
proposed <=16.7 ms nominal refresh spacing and immediate refresh on invalidation.
That design choice permits every-other-frame skips only around >=120 FPS; it
would take the original path in the present roughly 60 FPS scene. It is not a
universal perceptual threshold or a user-imposed quality gate. Relaxing it to
30 Hz without moving-caster/foliage quality evidence is not justified by fixed
benchmark stills.

Before implementation could be worth reopening: establish a material removable
shadow transaction cost, then actual unfrozen-world transform/caster invalidation
and guard fractions with the existing observer. Missing producer epochs remain
unknown. Test current map age and projected distorted shadow displacement;
refresh on camera motion/frustum coverage uncertainty, edits/uploads/resources,
day/night change, fast/unknown casters, image side effects and compatibility loss.
An exact input cache would fall back for unobserved animation/material producers;
an approximate cadence must explicitly accept and measure their visual delay.

Then an authorized coordinated clears/targets/matrix transaction could be tested
against original and disabled controls, with unfrozen clocks, near moving
silhouettes, leaves/grass, water/glass, entities/player, block actions, reload,
negative-grid crossings and stalls. No such implementation or runtime lane is
recommended now: source risks and weak measured budget justify fail-fast closure
while root pursues the pixel history quality work and other direct work budgets.

# Active user and agent lessons

Record demonstrated coordination failures with evidence, the agent's contribution
and a practical correction. Uncertainty and product disagreements are not confirmed
user errors. Keep this index short; preserve detailed episodes in linked history
or focused reports. Promote recurring mechanical failures into tested operations.

## Use actual dispatch state

A message to a completed native worker did not restart execution, repeatedly.
Use native `followup_task` or a fresh T3 `delegate_task` as appropriate, retain the
returned identity and verify acknowledgment/accepted state before reporting work
active. Each T3 review round is a new task; never message its backing child thread.
See [the runtime adapter](T3_AGENT_RUNTIME.md) and historical dispatch episodes
(lines 91–106, 1458–1465, 1613–1619, 1661–1668 in the archive below).

## Bind evidence to the actual consumer

Source/helper tests missed packaging, plugin registration, retired hash readers
and loader-specific joins. Exercise the actual public producer/compiled consumer
and installed resource inputs with authentic positive, mutation and recovery
cases. Inspect the first retained refusal, not an overwriteable final message.
Historical examples include normal observer registration (1707–1725), first
runtime refusal (1830–1862), compiled consumers (1864–1915) and shared-profile
packaging (1988–1997). Use existing focused tests for unchanged dependencies.

## Finish restore and release inside the operation

A finite diagnostic ended before native restoration; a terminated owned child
also remained a zombie until reaped. Include restore/verify/save/exact-stop/reap/
lock release in the executable completion path. Observe current state before
retrying an ambiguous failure. Read-only transport loss does not prove a remote
client stopped. See historical restoration/reaping episodes (1728–1766).

## Check prerequisite success and fresh run identity

A failed adoption preflight was followed by checks against old source; old log
readiness and stale test reports also appeared current. Sequence dependent work
only after actual success, inspect JSON success as well as exit status, and bind
readiness/results to fresh process/execution identities. See historical source
adoption (1959–1966), readiness (1951–1957) and test-denominator correction
(1819–1827). Equal hashes alone do not prove images decode (1622–1629).

## Keep measurement and completion claims scoped

A preview, source pass, RESTORED attempt or `FAMILY_COMPLETE` message did not prove
project/Full completion. Preserve all allocated unfinished families; independent
authorized work can continue alongside human feedback. Use one stdout reader per
operation and terminal metadata for explicit Full completion. Keep actual hardware,
scene, resolution, effective options, temporal inputs, motion quality and speed
limits attached to their evidence. See historical preview scope (1769–1782),
comparison mismatch (1917–1957) and duplicate monitoring (1978–1986).

## Coordinate shared personal settings before writing

On October 19 two project migrations edited the same global Codex hooks. This
ShaderLOD parent replaced a concurrent tested version after reading older bytes,
causing the other project's hook rerun to fail. Separate repository ownership did
not isolate shared personal files. After explicit human authorization, the parents
acknowledged one global owner in the Binary thread and froze competing writes;
ShaderLOD retained project-only ownership. Preserve snapshots and merge current
deltas through that owner, then verify the combined tests and normal runtime
activation. For future parallel setup tasks, establish the shared-file owner and
compare the immediately observed SHA before writing; do not assume project-local
worktrees isolate home-directory settings. No campaign or GPU ownership transfers.

## Verify the setting's actual consumer

The October 19 T3 migration registered five project actions through
`t3_project_update`; metadata reported them saved. An isolated child emitted a
generic workspace-ready message without a setup-script receipt. Inspection of
the installed 0.1.0 runner showed it reads folded settings overrides instead of
that metadata field. The agent initially treated metadata as registration and
corrected the claim before acceptance. Read the effective settings source and
exercise the real consumer; preserve the failed observation. The runtime adapter
records the affected version and action-resolution boundary. After the settings
owner merged the effective override, a fresh T3 worktree's exact setup terminal
showed the registered command, truthful missing-input report and completion exit
0 before model startup. The parent's direct terminal inspection resolved the
child's intentionally unproven generic receipt; no manual setup rerun was counted.

## Historical evidence

[Complete pre-migration lessons](USER_LESSONS.history-20261019.md) are preserved
byte-for-byte: 150,410 bytes, SHA-256
`b2085d961a200ef3beb3d4f033c7f89a6f19d5959026e24169a115ce0c799aa6`.
Line numbers above refer to that immutable snapshot. It remains in the original
directory, preserving relative links. Search the relevant episode rather than
loading all historical lessons for every task. Add a concise active entry only
when a new demonstrated issue changes the next decision or operation.

# PC package verification — 2026-10-17

The reviewed package payload is accepted for the scoped MC1.21.1 / NeoForge21.1.253 / Java21 implementation handoff. A documentation portability defect was found and accepted for repair by the parent; the regenerated archive requires the parent's checksum/delta verification. This review does not assert that regeneration has completed.

Reviewed archive: `dev/artifacts/ShaderLOD-PC-1.21.1-NeoForge.zip`, 20,657,739 bytes, SHA-256 `4e47966bf1c21ec8e63d01e1536d03c8e2e09564e0fc18c4695377ac19df3487`. All 35 ZIP members pass CRC, equal the staging directory byte for byte, and match its complete file inventory. All 33 manifest file hashes match; SHA256SUMS verifies 34 files including the manifest. The manifest excludes itself and SHA256SUMS, and SHA256SUMS excludes itself, as expected.

There are exactly three mod JARs: normal ShaderLOD, Iris1.8.12 and Sodium0.6.13. ShaderLOD hashes to `119662204d8ad1497deb86062497f40894037fd366f8b61b3f65cfd5b15720ea`, passes archive CRC and contains no development package entries. Iris/Sodium match their retained release SHA-1, SHA-512 and SHA-256 records. No driver-download or target-PC runtime verification was performed.

All nine shader ZIPs pass CRC, equal the actual declared original source files byte for byte, and match the original-archive pins in the three packaged readiness inventories. They are not generated ShaderLOD archives. Reference map sizes are Photon366, Solas428, AstraLex1015, Reimagined398, Unbound398, Bliss463, MakeUp100, Sildur115 and BSL384. These JSON maps are explicitly descriptive references, not supplied installable user settings. No Mac tuned profiles, generated shader ZIPs, worlds or development observer are included. Credits preserve upstream/source and private-transfer boundaries.

[The handoff](pc-implementation-handoff-20261017.md), package README and READINESS distinguish 549 source dispositions from distinct algorithms or wins, and source-declared applicable counts from actual runtime evidence. Six families have the retained normal-public-API runtime controls; Photon/Solas/AstraLex still require first successful PC driver rendering. Windows visual/motion, fresh FPS, DH and PBR acceptance remain pending. The normal Full functional operation is honestly INCOMPLETE0/67, not a winning profile or complete search. No earlier Mac percentages become PC presets. The still-image claim is explicitly attributed to the parent's limited inspection.

Concrete defect: `evidence/functional-review.md` retained twelve repository-relative Markdown links into unbundled `dev/logs`, `run-workloads` and `src` paths. Two targets already exist within the package and can be rebased (`final-build-receipt.json` and `independent-functional-review.json`); unbundled paths must be labelled source-checkout references rather than working archive links. The parent accepted this repair, plus the misleading READINESS “Download” wording pointing at manifest.json, and owns checksum/manifest/archive regeneration and delta verification. README and READINESS direct internal links otherwise resolved in the reviewed archive. This affects review portability, not mod/shader bytes.

The ignored [machine-readable review](../../dev/logs/pc-port-readiness-20261017/package-independent-review.json) records the reviewed pre-repair archive identity and per-family pin checks. No code, build, tests or clients were run; no source or package files were changed by this reviewer. All commands are released and no live processes are owned.

Final packaging delta independently accepted: regenerated ZIP SHA-256 `448eec7b692fda878926d3054a86d905f32af8fbb87db8fd68a7aeb24c3a7a9e`, 20,657,766 bytes. Compared with the preserved pre-portability archive: only Markdown, manifest.json and SHA256SUMS changed; all mod/shader/reference/evidence JSON bytes are unchanged. Rechecked all 35 final CRCs and staging equality, manifest hashes and SHA256SUMS, and found no unresolved local Markdown links. The twelve unbundled links are now rebased where possible or explicitly labelled source-checkout references. Documentation defect closed; no new source/build/runtime claim. Commands remain released.

# Benchmark guide

For the local Asahi machine without a desktop, see [headless development](HEADLESS.md).
The maintained Linux ARM64 launcher selects its installed GPU-backed virtual
display when no display is explicitly selected; the native 2560×1600 viewport
and all normal benchmark guards remain required.

Use the maintained command for discovery, planning, execution and results:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py discover
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py plan --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py check --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_CHECK_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py report --output REPORT
```

`discover` lists local managed slots, worlds and shader archives. It is an inventory, not compatibility approval. Use `--profile` instead of `--slot` for an explicit prepared client. Set `--width` and `--height` to the intended native viewport (the local Asahi fullscreen mode is 2560×1600). Select the exact original pack/options for the feature; private candidates use `--candidate` instead of `--feature`. See the [candidate reference](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md) for specialized scenes, compatibility checks and qualification protocols.

`plan` runs the standard test's static checks without compiling, launching or creating the report. It lists the resolved launch plan, schedule, per-check elapsed time, failures and remedies. A stale build is reported; `test` rebuilds it automatically before launch. Native options and canonical profile inputs are checked; preserve unexplained differences before resetting a managed slot. Runtime-only checks still run in the client.

`check` accepts the same candidate arguments and exercises activation, available source/work checks, short captures and restoration without the two-minute conditioning period. It reports no performance or visual qualification. Use it when checking whether a newly integrated candidate runs; use `test` for a development performance comparison. Frozen Bliss qualification cannot use `check`.

`test` uses the fixed native/candidate/native-return protocol described below. `report` reads existing reports without launching anything, including historical reports. Its decision gives drift comparison precedence over an averaged positive mean, and identifies invalid runs or recovery requirements. It does not grant optimization closure or compatibility qualification. Phase timings in `summary.json` include nested profile preparation/restoration details; do not sum nested details into the total again.

For optimization iteration use the maintained standard test, on the authorized machine with a prepared managed client slot and authentic original pack and options:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test \
  --profile /path/to/prepared/client \
  --pack /path/to/original-pack.zip \
  --pack-options /path/to/original-pack.zip.txt \
  --feature PUBLIC_OPTIMIZATION_ID \
  --output /path/to/fresh/report
```

The command automatically selects the existing Linux ARM64 launcher on that platform. Explicit `linux_arm64_runtime.py` commands remain supported. It finds an installed full JDK21 or a cached Gradle JDK21; an explicit JAVA_HOME retains precedence. Select an existing loader/version/scene slot; keep the report outside that slot and on the same filesystem as the profile. Confirm the lane is free and the inputs match the intended tuple before launch. Do not reset a slot owned by a client or interrupted operation. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py checkout --help` describes managed checkout. Use `run_storage.copytree` for profile/world copies; it enforces storage limits.

The standard test targets the prepared NeoForge 1.21.1 benchmark protocol. It renders native Off for 120 seconds before measurement, then acquires native Off, singleton candidate through normal Apply, then native Off return: 20 seconds each, with separate warmup, startup and recovery within a 900-second budget. Conditioning was added after repeated first-to-return drift; it does not prove stability. It records total-frame timing, drift, stills and restoration in the report. A valid slower result is still a result; a failed or invalid run is not a speed conclusion. Inspect `summary.json`, errors and restoration before proceeding. A short result is not proof of visual equivalence, DH/PBR compatibility or final closure. Compare matched total-frame measurements and disclose drift and scope.

# Native Windows benchmarking

The RTX 2080 Ti host DESKTOP-T4JKGJB has an isolated runtime under
`C:\ShaderLODBench`: repository snapshot `ShaderLOD`, original profile
`canonical-client`, portable tools in `tools`, and `gradle-cache`. The prepared
managed slot is `rtx2080ti-baseline`. Preserve these reusable inputs and caches.
This is a copied source tree, so synchronize intended changes before testing.

Launch native Windows Python and JDK21 in the logged-in user's interactive
console session. Launching Windows Java through WSL SSH runs in Session 0,
which cannot supply the required monitor. A manually started temporary Task
Scheduler task with an Interactive principal can enter the console session;
remove that task when finished. No automatic trigger is needed. Keep the
console unlocked and do not use the PC during capture. Readiness must confirm
hardware NVIDIA rendering, 2560×1600 native framebuffer, focus, and no fallback.

Set JAVA_HOME to the extracted JDK, GRADLE_USER_HOME to the isolated cache, and
put portable Python and Java's bin directory on PATH. Install the pinned
`requirements-dev.txt` dependencies for native Windows. The embeddable Python
path file must include the repository and its scripts directory. PowerShell
must not treat ordinary native stderr as a terminating exception; inspect the
native process exit code and the completed report instead.

Use the maintained commands in [the benchmark guide](BENCHMARK.md). A matched
native variability block uses:

```powershell
python scripts/run_benchmark.py test --slot rtx2080ti-baseline `
  --pack 'dependencies/upstream/pack-expansion/Bliss_v2.1.2_(Chocapic13_Shaders_edit).zip' `
  --pack-options dev/experiments/new-optimization-goals-20261102/bliss-native463.txt `
  --candidate n04-bliss-sky --scene saved --saved-pose 0 `
  --width 2560 --height 1600 --bliss-qualification null `
  --qualification-order ABBA --qualification-client-heap 1536m `
  --output dev/experiments/FRESH_REPORT
```

The maintained qualification protocol supplies 180 seconds of conditioning,
20 seconds of settling and four 60-second windows; do not override its schedule.
Repeat with BAAB and a new output path. A and B are byte-identical original
shaders. This measures apparent gains caused by noise; it tests no optimization.
Check validity, source/graph identity, configuration restoration, world reset,
and zero remaining clients before interpreting results. Two blocks describe
this session, not a universal noise threshold or cross-hardware speedup.

Windows process ownership uses native psutil cwd/argument-vector observations
and exact process birth identities, including NeoForge argument-file evidence.
World restoration holds Java-compatible locks and preserves the world root and
session.lock in place, because Windows prevents renaming their open parent
directory. Exact canonical input maps are checked afterward. Existing slots
with world locks should be reused through the maintained runner; generic
whole-slot checkout replacement is not verified for Windows.

Control results are published atomically only after completion, with a separate
CREATE_NEW pending marker preventing command replay. Published receipts remain
immutable, avoiding Windows read/replace sharing races. Recovery does not replay
uncertain commands. Mutable Python records retry only transient Windows
file-sharing errors for at most three seconds; they never repeat the associated
Minecraft command. Persistent access errors still fail and require recovery.

NVIDIA temperature, clocks, utilization and power are endpoint snapshots.
Windows memory observations include working set, private commit and total page
faults; Linux PSI, cgroup and separate minor/major fault counters are unavailable,
not zero. These observations do not establish absence of thermal throttling.

# User and agent lessons

Record only demonstrated coordination problems or corrected misunderstandings.
Use context, evidence, agent contributions, and a practical lesson. Keep the
record respectful; uncertainty and product disagreements are not confirmed
user errors.

## October12 second audit: dimension and parser assumptions still need real consumers

The End-cloud candidate initially inherited an Overworld Performance-routing
annotation. Both author and first reviewer missed that all ten renderer routes
require Overworld; parent traced the actual gate and a fresh candidate-r2 corrected
the metadata. Explicit Apply in End can select generated Performance, while portal
reselection and native End rendering remain unverified. The original receipt is
preserved. The new Iris utility also initially trusted MutableOptionValues to
validate string ranges; an independent actual-BSL mutation disproved that assumption.
It now checks Iris's declared allowed values, with a regression. Parent's streaming
hash helper initially changed a provider exception into AssertionError; reviewer
caught the escaped refusal path and parent restored the checked exception, tested
with provider removal in a disposable JVM. These were agent integration mistakes.
Trace the actual consumer's dimension/value/error behavior once, then reuse that
tested operation. [Evidence and corrections](DEVELOPMENT_THROUGHPUT_REVIEW_20261012.md#second-investigation-parallelism-and-useful-work).

Offline delivery follow-up, October12: parent and the first carry source review
verified the generic recipe/catalog consumer before tracing NeoForge26.2's
separate source certificate. Its exact old recipe pin would refuse the new
generated graph. The joint check retained that refusal, and the isolated overlay
now includes only the matching certificate pin update; every other validation
guard remains unchanged. The maintained
[combined consumer test](../tests/test_offline_delivery_integration.py) exercises
the actual loader-specific source certificate as well as selection/recovery.
This repeats the consumer-join omission above; the parent and review scope
contributed. No runtime failure or user mistake is attributed. The same pass
also found the methods audit's prior-weight proposal had an already-closed
no-gain trial; that negative evidence remains closed and linked in the
[focused assessment](evaluation/complementary-prior-weight-reasoning-20261012.md).

## Choose the target ecosystem before inheriting build versions

On 2026-10-03, the agent initially adopted the neighboring mod's Minecraft
26.1.2 target because the runtime dependencies existed. The user then clarified
that broad adoption should determine the first target. Current pack releases
and version-download evidence supported NeoForge 1.21.1, so setup was migrated
before acceptance. Reuse build infrastructure independently of its version pins;
check the audience criterion before selecting dependencies. Compatibility alone
does not establish popularity. This was an agent assumption corrected by the
user, not a user mistake.

## Separate a visual preview from a performance sanity check

The first side-by-side scene demonstrated controls and quality zones, but its
sparse geometry, substantial sky, and Photon early-outs made it a weak PCF
performance workload. When the user reported equal/slightly lower LOD FPS,
the source audit found little medium-tier work to remove. Explain effect scope
and actual baseline work before presenting a performance comparison. Label the
right-hand client accurately: it retained ShaderLOD with LOD disabled after the
user requested restoring the previous windows; the mod-absent baseline was not
completed. Keep live windows available while investigating read-only.

## Prioritize visual value over the number of effects modified

On2026-10-04 the user observed missing shadows on distant trees and rejected
the aggressive profile's roughly0.5ms saving as poor value. The agent had noticed
flatter distant foliage in captures but emphasized implemented effects and timing
results without clearly flagging that visual cost. Far AO was bypassed despite
its whole pass costing only0.057ms in the earlier profile; screen-space shadows
also became extremely sparse. Preserve important low-frequency lighting cues,
use effect-specific importance criteria, and evaluate quality alongside time.
Passing compilation/runtime checks and measuring a gain do not establish a
worthwhile optimization or a shipping-quality preset.

## Verify effective and temporal shader inputs

During the sustained goal on 2026-10-04, the initial repeated runner compared
option-file bytes. Iris normalized those files by removing defaults and adding
comments, so the guard rejected a semantically unchanged baseline. The benchmark
worker corrected verification to read loaded Iris option values and retain raw
hashes as separate evidence. Preserve failed captures instead of silently
relabeling them as performance results.

Further source auditing by the shader worker found that fixed rain/day time do
not fully specify Photon clouds: Iris smooths wetness and Photon uses it for
weather humidity and wind. Fresh clear saves switched to rain can initialize
differently from reused rainy saves. Actual wetness was not logged in the first
36-run matrix, so the proposed explanation remains unverified in those captures.
Record effective options and relevant temporal uniforms, inspect initialization,
and verify steady inputs before claiming a matched cloud workload. Frame count
alone and a fixed warmup duration do not prove that every shader input settled.

# Benchmark guide

For the local Asahi machine without a desktop, see [headless development](HEADLESS.md).
The maintained Linux ARM64 launcher selects its installed GPU-backed virtual
display when no display is explicitly selected; the native 2560×1600 viewport
and all normal benchmark guards remain required.

For the prepared RTX 2080 Ti Windows host, see [Windows benchmarking](WINDOWS_BENCHMARK.md).

Use the maintained command for discovery, planning, execution and results:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py discover
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py baseline --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --output FRESH_BASELINE
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py plan --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py check --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_CHECK_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py report --output REPORT
```

separately variance/SD of the three window means and first-to-last drift.

variation. Keep absent-mod baselines separate from the matched Master-Off
controls in optimization comparisons. Startup failure supplies no frame-time
measurement. `native-startup` remains a short original-only startup diagnostic.

or capabilities. Explicit requests disable NeoForge's reusable early window in

`plan` runs the standard test's static checks without compiling, launching or creating the report. It lists the resolved launch plan, schedule, per-check elapsed time, failures and remedies. ## Choose the check for the question

| Question | Maintained route | What it does not establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What inputs and candidates exist? | `discover`, then `plan` with selected inputs | Runtime compatibility or ownership |
| Does this change activate and recover? | `check` | Performance or visual equivalence |
| Is the idea worth more investigation? | `test`, then `report` | Broad workload/machine qualification |
| What does native do without ShaderLOD? | `baseline` | Installed-Off overhead by itself |
| Does it preserve motion or work across packs/hardware? | Candidate-specific protocols in the reference | Coverage of untested scenes, transitions or machines |

Before designing a new study, establish the user's intended decision: deep
workload performance, compatibility breadth, quality, or a quick screen. Reuse
the supported commands above. Put the chosen claim, comparator, coverage, useful
metrics, controls and budget in the existing experiment record. Record exclusions
and fallback separately; do not impose a universal repetition count or payback
horizon. Performance requires actual-window execution and valid output evidence,
not merely enabling a setting. Source changes do not inherit earlier timings.

## Records and milestone cleanup

Keep current work in STATUS, durable attempts/decisions in EXPERIMENTS, supported
procedures here and specialized routes in BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES. Extend the existing
candidate entry when adding a route; retire superseded wrappers only after checking
imports, tests and historical reproduction dependencies. Keep active experiments in
`dev/experiments`, reusable inputs/clients in `dependencies` and `run-workloads`,
and retained historical evidence in `experiment-evidence`. Do not move a pinned

After an investigation, preserve compact raw measurements, configuration/source

### P1: output-history coordinate must preserve the output lattice

approximation across the current footprint; expected previous depth and surface
validity must be defined at `h`, not inadvertently retained at the old `p`.

# Named tunings and independent tuning goals

Architecture/current-contract map for the newly authorized reusable tuning system. Root owns product integration, normal UI and the exclusive build/client lane. `tuner_repair` owns the goal/search integration below. Source work is not actual activation, image fidelity or performance evidence. The prior functional Full result0/67 exercised failure/restoration, not completed search, a saved winner or named-library activation.

## Existing boundaries to reuse

`BenchmarkScreen` → `BenchmarkUi` → `AutoTuner` is the ordinary client entry and private demo lifecycle. `OptimizationScreen` already stages a complete independent-request vector and discards it on Cancel. `ShaderLodSettingsScreen` owns normal core settings. `OptimizationConfig` stores one current vector per family; it is not a named library. `TuningJournal` persists the original core/request/video state before mutation, raw clocks/decisions, final actual configuration and pending recovery. `TuningContinuation` carries bounded inventory coverage and a prior SAVED incumbent, not old timing decisions. `TuningSourceIdentity` is strict **local** original/generated/state-pair recovery authority; it must not become a portable filename exemption.

Public Apply remains `ShaderLodSettings.apply` plus `OptimizationEditTransaction.apply(..., CompileOptionControl::open)` and the same two-phase selection transaction, pending queues, consumer finish and guarded recovery. Root's named Apply service owns its separate durable pending/Undo record and must refuse a tuner/timing owner; tuner start/Undo now refuse a pending named Apply. An Apply failure is not acknowledged until current graph/core/request/scene recovery completes. The retained parked tuner job keeps an unacknowledged SceneLease and blocks new tuning/Exit; explicit Undo retries that owner.

## Data and normal user flow

The concrete root model is `TuningPreset`: UUID-managed ID and display name; family and exact original executable-source hash; enabled and actual engine LodPreset; complete raw near/far/transition/debug; all61 canonical request values; exact original-domain native shader values; complete per-effect requested mode/bands/medium/far/protection values; context; evidence; creation time. The semantic configuration digest includes the full settings, requests and binding, not merely enabled IDs or display name. Versioned UTF-8 JSON is bounded and atomically stored; unknown/missing flag or field/schema values are refused. UUID filenames separate user names from paths.

Root normal service/API: capture/saveCurrent, list, rename, clone/edit via existing staged controls, compatibility preview, Apply, Undo, import and export. Save Current creates MANUAL evidence; a staged edit is not active until ordinary Apply. An edited variant or import cannot inherit local measured-winner status. Rename may retain evidence because it does not change the semantic configuration digest. The normal UI should distinguish current active configuration from a selected saved record and show family, goal versus actual engine mode, provenance, compatibility and unreviewed image quality.

Imports preserve settings/provenance as imported-unverified and get a new managed identity. Source/native mismatch refuses automatic Apply. Device/context mismatch is not authority to bypass runtime guards; compatible settings may be tried manually, but old speed/default claims are not local evidence. Portable files carry content identities and native values, never trusted absolute paths to another machine's generated archive or state file. The current selected source supplies a fresh local strict pair. Export includes a portable tuning and optionally its bounded retained evidence members, without worlds or downloaded shader archives.

**Important integration join:** current generated option maps contain parser/helper declarations in addition to the native option domain. Stripping compile graph controls alone does not produce native398/native100/etc. The separate `TuningNativeOptions.project` assignment must verify the real original/generated pair and full generated effective map using authentic Iris parsers, then project actual values to the original domain. `SavedTunings.nativeOptions` and `final.native_option.*` use that normalized domain. AutoTuner's existing full graph-pin map remains unchanged; no SHADERLOD-prefix exemption or dropped fingerprint is introduced.

`SavedTunings.recordValidated(runDirectory, flags, goal)` is called only after actual final Apply, scene-close acknowledgment and `journal.finish(SAVED)` have closed final raw evidence. It checks current full configuration against per-key final metadata and binds hashes of metadata/decisions/samples/original Undo. No successful-hook metadata rewrite may invalidate those hashes. A named-save I/O failure is separately diagnosed and cannot manufacture a failed timing result or erase SAVED. MEASURED_LOCAL means measured configuration under its context, **not** visually certified. The evidence visual-review field remains UNREVIEWED.

## Independent goals, engine modes and complete-vector proof

New API: `TuningRequest(TuningGoal goal, int budgetSeconds, boolean full)` and `AutoTuner.start(request)`. Existing start(seconds,full) delegates PERFORMANCE. Existing finite Quick/Full limits remain; no new clock or statistical threshold is introduced. `TuningGoal.label()` and `enginePreset()` are available to root's tier selector/commands.

| Performance | PERFORMANCE | Source-declared and currently applicable requests; unknown declarations skipped explicitly |
| Balanced | BALANCED | Explicit conservative conventional detail/budget/refinement set plus reviewed exact requests; existing Performance-only CPU renderer requests excluded |
| Quality — exact changes only | PERFORMANCE | Reviewed exact-only six-ID set: compaction, admission/scalar caches, binding certificate/digest controls and zero-emission arithmetic |

`LodPreset.QUALITY` and ordinal3 remain native graph/full work. A useful exact-only search cannot use engine QUALITY while existing CPU renderer admission requires engine PERFORMANCE. The separate approved search goal therefore uses PERFORMANCE with only the explicit exact request policy. This does not redefine the existing native Quality setting. Mixed semantic IDs such as reflection/depth reuse are not assumed exact across all families; admitting them to this goal needs separate source qualification and a policy revision.

No tier is assembled by unioning individual wins or relabeling a Performance result. ## Four decisive live acceptance slices

## Link, deletion and text-packing chain

1. Exact `SodiumPrograms.transformShaders(ProgramSource, AlphaTest, ProgramSet)`
   obtains a `Map<PatchShaderType, String>` from `TransformPatcher.patchSodium`.
   At bytecode 72–94 it passes this same map to
   `ShaderPrinter.printProgram(...).addSources(map).print()`, then returns it.
   `ProgramPrintBuilder.addItem`
   stores the supplied String unchanged; `print` calls `Files.writeString` at
   bytecode 185. No extra newline/header is appended to the source content.
2. `SodiumPrograms.createGlShaders(String, Map)` iterates that map and passes each
   non-null String unchanged to the Sodium constructor
   `GlShader(ShaderType, ResourceLocation, String)` at bytecode 113. This is not
   Iris's different generic `gl.shader.GlShader` implementation.
3. Sodium's `GlShader` constructor calls `ShaderWorkarounds.safeShaderSource`
   at bytecode 21, then compiles and checks compile status. The workaround encodes
   that String with `MemoryUtil.memUTF8(source, true)` and calls
   `GL20C.nglShaderSource(shader, 1, pointer, 0)` at bytecode 32: one UTF-8,
   NUL-terminated source string, with a null lengths pointer. There is no
   additional define insertion, ShaderConstants pass or source concatenation in
   this constructor path.
4. `SodiumPrograms.createShader(...)` attaches every constructed shader through
   `GlProgram.Builder.attachShader(GlShader)`, then calls `buildProgram`.
   `GlProgram.Builder.link(Function)` calls `glLinkProgram` at bytecode 4,
   checks `GL_LINK_STATUS`, and constructs the result at bytecode 68–80.
   It contains **no detach call**. The wrapper constructor runs its binding
   factory after assigning the program's numeric handle; the inspected factory
   creates uniforms/samplers/the `SodiumShader` interface and does not detach.
5. `createShader` runs its shader-deletion consumer on both normal and exception
   exits. Verbose bootstrap metadata identifies that consumer exactly as
   `REF_invokeVirtual ...sodium...GlShader.delete:()V`.
   `GlShader.delete()` is `glDeleteShader(handle)` followed by
   `invalidateHandle()`, with no detach. Java `GlObject.handle()` thereafter
   throws for that invalidated wrapper; the GL attachment is separate.

The OpenGL API keeps a shader marked for deletion alive while attached to any
program. `glGetAttachedShaders` returns those attached IDs, and
`glGetShaderSource` returns the source previously supplied to the shader object.
This is why deletion status true is expected and is not a rejection by itself.
[Khronos deletion semantics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/OpenGL-Refpages/main/gl4/glDeleteShader.xml),
[attachment query](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/OpenGL-Refpages/main/gl4/glGetAttachedShaders.xml),
[source query](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KhronosGroup/OpenGL-Refpages/main/gl4/glGetShaderSource.xml).

## Naming, lifecycle and failure guards

The full fragment hash uniquely joins the current submitted program to the
specific transformed export in this qualification. The exact existing named
program route is also public and can provide a direct numeric cross-check:

```java
WorldRenderingPipeline.getSodiumPrograms() -> SodiumPrograms
SodiumPrograms.getProgram(DefaultTerrainRenderPasses.TRANSLUCENT) -> GlProgram<ChunkShaderInterface>
GlProgram.handle() -> int
```

`IrisRenderingPipeline.getSodiumPrograms()` returns its stored object directly.
`SodiumPrograms.getProgram(TerrainRenderPass)` maps the supplied pass to its enum
then returns the program map entry. **The mapping is shadow-state-sensitive**:
for TRANSLUCENT it selects `SHADOW_TRANS` during shadow rendering and
`TRANSLUCENT` otherwise. Explicitly require
`!ShadowRenderingState.areShadowsCurrentlyBeingRendered()` before naming a draw
as ordinary water/translucent. Enum TRANSLUCENT's original ID is `ProgramId.Water`,
but the constructor also uses `ProgramFallbackResolver.resolveNullable`; the
enum name alone cannot prove which source won. A full expected source hash
provides that missing source identity. Null pipeline/program, invalid Java handle
or mismatch against `GL_CURRENT_PROGRAM` stays unknown/native.

Record the session/profile, fresh pack/options/JAR pins, pipeline identity or
generation, frame, actual current program ID, attachment count/IDs/stage/status,
source byte length/hash and expected export identity. Recheck current program
after the getters. Readback succeeds only if the expected program remains bound,
link and compile status are successful, the fragment is unique, and complete
source bytes equal the explicit expected arm. The retained native program path
does not resubmit source or relink after construction; if runtime code does either,
that lifecycle needs a new join. Getter output by itself does not attest an
unobserved later relink or source mutation.

The probe's existing global `SEEN<Integer>` survives reloads and numeric GL IDs
can be reused. Do not claim reload safety from that set. The smallest safe scope
is one fresh JVM/one frozen pipeline/no reload; otherwise reset/partition the
capture by actual pipeline generation. Likewise a first unrelated quad capture
must not suppress the required raster-origin record merely because it inserted
an ID into `SEEN`. Preserve the actual draw origin and terminate a missing-source
capture as unknown instead of accepting a uniform resemblance.

If a driver returns no attachments, zero/oversized/truncated source, more than one
fragment, invalid IDs or a mismatched hash, keep the raw receipt and stop that
join. That outcome would disagree with the expected pinned lifecycle and must
not be silently replaced with a heuristic. The named-program getter can still
establish program-map identity, **not attached source identity** by itself.
If constructor capture becomes necessary, the narrow additional seam is
`GlProgram.Builder.link(Function) RETURN`: its returned program is linked while
the shaders are still live, before Iris's `createShader` deletion consumer.
Capture its fragment hash there and carry the exact returned program plus
pipeline lifetime to the existing raster hook. This is a contingency, not a
recommended new hook for the current proven attachment lifecycle; unknown JARs
or a changed detach/link lifecycle require fresh inspection first.

Even a successful source/draw join establishes only that a submitted terrain
program contains the intended water branch. It does **not** measure material
32000 coverage, fragment invocations, whether a particular water pixel traversed
or hit terrain, discarded/occluded work, diagnostic quality, fallback costs or
performance. Preserve the original/removal/return image and coverage gates.

## What the new addon can cost with no active extension users

Current `EffectUniformsMixin` registers 37 PER_FRAME fields plus one
`EffectUniformFrame` notifier listener per registration group. Every notifier
callback clears a reference even if no effect supplier is consumed. Registration
allocations/location lookups belong to pipeline construction and warmup;
callback delivery remains per frame.

Pinned Iris bytecode establishes that `ProgramUniforms.Builder.location` returns
empty for location −1, and `LocationalUniformHolder.uniform1i/uniform1f` only adds
the uniform through `OptionalInt.ifPresent`. `ProgramUniforms.update` updates
linked PER_FRAME uniforms when its frame counter changes. The custom-expression
path initially retains input suppliers, but `CustomUniforms.optimise` removes
unused dependency nodes; IrisRenderingPipeline calls it during construction,
then calls notifier.onNewFrame before customUniforms.update while rendering.

`EffectUniformFrame.control` snapshots all six effects only when a supplier
queries it; subsequent suppliers in that registration group reuse the snapshot
until the callback clears it. Original Photon and B15 contain no extension
consumer names. Thus avoiding per-effect snapshots for those packs is supported
by source expectations, while unconditional notifier overhead remains. There
are no runtime addon supplier counts here. Do not claim zero overhead or that
absence of extension consumers proves an inactive mixin.

Global enable false/true never disables the addon registration/listener. Both AO
patched arms used the same new main classes and INHERIT/unity/protected effect
config SHA256 `c02b81bc4ad7c90ac2e23e839845ddcfa8d7ab6909a380161f319ed414530984`.
Their difference cannot isolate addon cost. Likewise, config mode FULL or
INHERIT is not an addon-disable switch. A pure addon-only ablation would need
a separate reviewed source/build change; no such existing switch or microtimer
was found. Return that optional choice to root instead of expanding the harness.

## B10 — nonblocking current-depth queries have a bounded design, not a pilot

The portable candidate remains possible on GL 4.1; missing compute/SSBO/MDI does
not reject it. The [ARB boolean occlusion-query specification](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/ARB/ARB_occlusion_query2.txt)
defines results over samples that pass depth, with an availability state. This
is algorithm/API evidence; a query object or result was not observed here.

A defensible ordering is: render an eligible near-occluder subset natively in the
**current** view; query conservative bounds for disjoint remaining opaque
candidates against that unchanged depth generation; continue independent work;
at the original submission decision, skip only if that exact query is available
and zero. Not-ready, changed depth/projection, resource replacement or unknown
bounds draws natively. Never spin, block for QUERY_RESULT, infer current hidden
from an old result, or fill a depth hole with stale geometry. An earlier *partial*
current depth buffer is conservative when it only omits valid occluders; it may
reduce culling success. Overfilled false coverage is unsafe.

Bounds must contain actual displaced geometry and conservative clipped raster
coverage, with a safe near-plane/camera-inside fallback and depth-test policy.
Ordinary 16³ section bounds do not certify pack waving/POM/clip offsets. Query
state must suppress its own color/depth/stencil writes and restore native state;
the tested source program must be free of side effects removed by skipping its
draw. Vanilla and DH depths cannot be mixed without their actual common
projection/encoding contract. Exclude translucent/order-sensitive draws,
entities and shadow/GI producer side effects from a first opaque contract.
The query certifies only current **main-view** visibility. As a geometric
counterexample, a 10 m tall off-camera caster with 10° sun elevation can cast a
ground shadow about `10 / tan(10°) = 56.7 m` toward visible ground. Main-view zero
does not authorize dropping its shadow draw. Photon shadow vertex code can also
voxelize before raster clipping (`program/shadow.vsh:89–97`); a main-view query
does not certify those image writes. B7 CPU replay retains all those GPU draws.

This design may split Sodium's region batches into many extra queries and draws.
With `Q` queried candidates and `Z` available-zero results, saving requires
`sum(work_removed_for_Z) > Q × query/bounds_cost + extra_submission + polling +
state_restore`. GPU/CPU overlap and availability can make `Z` nearly zero even
when many objects are hidden. No measurements establish the premise.
**Next cheap predicate:** source-qualify one conservative opaque bound and join
its actual current depth attachment/generation after existing near native draws,
then an untimed query-only/no-skip sample records availability at the unmodified
decision point. If it arrives late or the displaced bound is unknown, do not
build a culling cache or add a prepass merely to rescue it.

**B11:** screen silhouette distance alone does not bound Minecraft appearance.
An ostensibly coplanar merge can stretch atlas UVs, change triangle interpolation
of vertex AO/light/color, collapse material IDs, lose tangent handedness or
mid-UV tile identity, or move a waving top-vertex boundary. Photon explicitly
consumes material mask, tangent, mc_Entity and mc_midTexCoord in
`gbuffers_all_solid.vsh:19–43,99–155`; the nine terrain paths above likewise

interpolated/flat consumer under the actual triangulation, not just coplanarity.

resource/atlas reloads, edits, neighbor rebuilds, section removal and proxy

distant terrain representation; native-DH overlap and transition costs must be
subtracted, and users without DH must retain a valid native path.

amortized_build/upload + storage/streaming + transition_cost`; a CPU proxy may

Let `K` be required view/light slices, `A` their texel area, `b` bytes/texel,

# Terminal loaded-water scene survey

`WaterSceneSurvey.captureTerminalSnapshot(Minecraft client)` is an opt-in,
development-only read-only survey. It can help choose source-surveyed camera
anchors for targeted water tests. It does not establish glints, unobstructed
views, continuous water depth, shader quality, performance or safe underwater
camera placement. Compilation, actual survey execution and image/scene checks
belong to the root runtime owner. The author launched no client.

## Fixed cells, load guards and bounds

The candidate grid is exactly x `[240,300,400,500,650]`, z `[640,660,680]`,
y `[40..80]` inclusive: 15 columns and 615 candidate cells. Coordinates are
world block units; camera position is actual main-camera doubles and rotations
are degrees. No x260 column was added; x300/x400 may provide usable surveyed
alternatives, but that remains unverified until the report and scene are read.

Every world-state read first checks `client.level.hasChunkAt(pos)` **and**
`client.level.getChunkSource().hasChunk(x >> 4, z >> 4)`. This double guard is
necessary: Minecraft 1.21.1 `ClientLevel.hasChunk(int,int)` returns true
unconditionally. `ChunkSource.hasChunk` delegates to
`ClientChunkCache.getChunk(..., ChunkStatus.FULL, false)`, which returns null
for an absent/out-of-range cache entry without loading or generating terrain.
The survey never directly calls `getChunk`, requests server chunks, or uses a
heightmap. Missing chunks/out-of-build-range cells are unknown, never synthetic
AIR/water/empty terrain.

A loaded-only `BlockGetter` facade provides a cache shared by column cells,
camera context and any neighbor-dependent fluid-height/solid/collision getters.
It permits at most 4096 direct `ClientLevel.getBlockState` calls; each cached
immutable state also supplies its fluid state. All neighbor reads receive the
same double guard and budget. Block-entity-dependent context is unknown because
the facade deliberately declines that lookup. A known basic block/fluid record
remains known if a contextual shape/height field becomes unknown. The report
exposes actual direct read and unique cached-position counts, and budget status.
Biome sampling is omitted to avoid hidden neighboring lookups.

Actual `Camera.getFluidInCamera()` is called at most once. The exact cached
source reads the eye cell, up to five near-plane cells, and water/lava height
checks may read the cell above each. Before calling it, the survey guards and
preloads all six possible cells plus their above cells: at most 12 unique
positions. Its internal repeated block/fluid lookups are not instrumented;
17 is a conservative source-derived upper bound. The total world-state getter
call ceiling is therefore 4096 direct facade misses +17 camera-internal reads
=4113, not a silently claimed 615 total reads. All possible camera lookup
positions have been preloaded into the same bounded cache first. No FogType
query runs if its positions are missing/unavailable or the camera is not
initialized in the current camera-entity client level.
The camera-internal bound applies to the inspected Minecraft Camera method and
vanilla water/lava height implementations in the pinned development stack;
mods replacing those implementations require a fresh audit.

The terminal JSON records dimension, game/day time, day-time modulo 24000,
sky-light/ceiling flags, rain/thunder values at interpolation partial tick zero,
and current rain/thunder booleans. These are world inputs, not shader wetness

# Explicit, reversible pack selection

2026-10-06. CPU/source milestone. Root owns loader integration, Iris reloads,
client/GPU and runtime acceptance. No Gradle, client, GPU or commit was started
by the service worker.

`PackSelectionService` is a loader-independent explicit settings-Apply action:

```java
var result = new PackSelectionService().apply(
    shaderpacksDirectory, selectedPackFilename, lodEnabled,
    effectiveOriginalShaderOptions);
if (result.accepted()) {
    // Loader owner selects result.packFile(), saves Iris config, and reloads.
}
```

The three-argument overload reads the installed quality sidecar and the pinned
Photon defaults. The optional fourth argument carries actual effective/unsaved
options when an **original** pack is selected; it is intentionally ignored for
a generated selection so introduced TAAU options cannot become the original
quality state. The loader must persist pending generated-pack option changes to
its `.zip.txt` sidecar before Apply. Serialize actions through one loader owner.
There are no Minecraft, Iris, NeoForge or Fabric dependencies, downloads, watchers,
heuristic shader rewrites or automatic generation on source detection.

`Result` carries `status`, target `packFile`, `adapterId`, `generatedArchive`,
`optionsChanged`, and `detail`. `accepted()` includes APPLIED/UNCHANGED;
`requiresReload()` is true for APPLIED. UNSUPPORTED and REFUSED retain the supplied
selection. The loader retains its existing pack/config on either result and
reports the detail. A preset-only change still requires the loader's pipeline
reload even when pack selection returns UNCHANGED: these helpers use temporal
inputs which require a fresh graph after controls change.

## Photon On and Off

Native original Photon has TAA enabled and TAAU disabled, despite its latent
TAAU scale default of 0.75. On adds the private switch in a separate adapter and
sets TAAU=true with a selected stock scale of 1.00 **in that adapter sidecar**.
If original TAA was disabled, On preserves it and the latent TAAU flag/scale,
and disables the pixel budget. Older forced-TAA ownership migrates on explicit
Apply, rather than ordinary startup; see PHOTON_PRESET_PRESERVATION_R1.md.
Originally enabled
TAA+TAAU preserves its chosen scale, such as 0.50. The common helper caps this
stock scale at the mod preset budget; it does not replace the quality preset.
Invalid booleans/scales and the excluded Photon Voxy graph fail safely.

Off returns the original pack filename, restoring its actual graph. It reverses
only values which still equal the service's introduced overrides; user changes
to other options, and edits to an introduced value, survive. A previously chosen
latent scale is restored when its service override remains unchanged. On/Off/On
reuses the same generated copy, and two installed originals keep separate state.
The three SSR recipes need only `SHADERLOD_REFINEMENT_ADAPTER=1` in their generated
sidecars; Off similarly selects the original and removes only the introduced
value. DH/Voxy exclusion and shader behavior are the retained recipe contracts,
not new runtime evidence.

Each original filename has a stable `.shaderlod-selection-*.json` record in the
shaderpacks directory, containing original/generated filenames and full archive
hashes, recipe identity, active state, original quality map and necessary owned
overrides. Exact initial original sidecar bytes are saved as Base64, or ABSENT,
before any necessary quality-sidecar write. The backup is never overwritten.
An unchanged original sidecar remains byte-for-byte unchanged, including its
absence. Necessary merges preserve unrelated comments, escaping, ordering and
continuation lines. Simultaneous conflicting original/adapter option edits
refuse the action without writes. Older manual generated archives with no record
cannot establish their prior quality graph and are never silently adopted.

File replacements are atomic individually. This is not a multi-file filesystem
transaction: an I/O failure or process termination can leave a prepared state
or incomplete generated output. A later Apply validates recorded archive hashes
and fails safely rather than guessing. Loader integration owns rollback if Iris
selection/save/reload fails; snapshot the affected sidecars and selection state
before Apply, restore the previous Iris selection/config, and report the error.
Do not delete the original archive or silently reset personal settings.

# Runtime adapter extension API

An explicit adapter can now join the production Iris runtime without editing
Photon or the mixin. `IrisAdapterRuntime.register(descriptor, sources, exports)`
registers its declaration, independently pinned source bindings and exact
operation-to-uniform exports during client startup. Photon remains the sole
supported reference; registering a descriptor does not establish shader support.
The pure [adapter contract](LOD_ADAPTER_CONTRACT.md) and
[source/runtime binding contract](LOD_ADAPTER_BINDING.md) still apply.

## Startup registration

Call the API before Iris starts the first `generalCommonUniforms` registration.
The mixin seals at that method's HEAD, before core/effects/capability suppliers
bind. Its existing tail callbacks also seal when invoked independently. The
production runtime takes one immutable descriptor/source/export/option-key
snapshot and uses it for all subsequent pipelines and shader reloads.
Registration after that boundary throws `IllegalStateException` with an explicit
startup requirement. There is no hot adapter registration or cache invalidation.
An early `IrisAdapterRuntime.snapshot()` returns unavailable without sealing.

For example, client initialization can declare the following operation and
register independently reviewed source bindings:

```java
var operation = new WorkKey(Effect.REFLECTIONS,
        "example:reflection_steps", WorkKind.COUNT);
var descriptor = new AdapterDescriptor(
        new AdapterIdentity("example:reference", "exact-reviewed-revision"),
        List.of(new ProtocolRequirement("shaderlod:core", Set.of(2)),
                new ProtocolRequirement("shaderlod:effects", Set.of(2)),
                new ProtocolRequirement("shaderlod:capabilities", Set.of(1))),
        List.of(new WorkCapability(operation, new WorkCapability.CountFloor(1))));
// reviewedSources is a List<SourceBinding> with this exact descriptor identity,
// full container digests, exact consuming member digests and required Iris options.
IrisAdapterRuntime.register(descriptor, reviewedSources,
        List.of(new CapabilityExport(operation, "shaderlodExampleReflectionAvailable")));
```

This is an API example, not a new supported pack or shader consumer. Registration
does not discover classes or packs, rewrite GLSL, or infer support from names.
The runtime still reads selected source bytes only during pack registration and
checks effective loaded Iris options at the existing frame boundary.

`AdapterRegistration` is the independently usable composition facade. Its
`seal()` method returns the same immutable snapshot on each call;
`Sealed.bind(runtimeAccess, sourceReader)` creates an explicit binding. Production
initialization delegates reference declarations to `ReferenceComposition` inside
`IrisAdapterRuntime`; the generic lifecycle and resolver have no Photon branches.
The pinned `PhotonReferenceAdapter` sources are unchanged.

Spatial adapters can also pass an optional `RuntimeLayoutRequirement` through
`IrisAdapterRuntime.register(descriptor, reviewedSources, exports, requirement)`.
The requirement declares formats, quantity roles, pass groups and a rendered-size
domain. The shared frame snapshot caches validation per pack identity and actual
rendered dimensions; unavailable or incompatible dimensions return availability
0. Existing three-argument registrations retain their semantics. A declaration
does not verify physical images or feedback safety. See
[layout binding](SPATIAL_REFERENCE_BINDING.md) for the first explicit consumer.

## Validation and shared exports

Registration is atomic: a rejected bundle leaves no descriptor, source or export
behind. The API rejects:

- Duplicate exact adapter identities, including identical repeat declarations.
- Source bindings naming another descriptor identity, or any repeated full source
  digest within or across registrations. One source must resolve unambiguously.
- Missing runtime protocols or incompatible explicit accepted versions. Production
  offers core 2, effects 2 and capabilities 1. Every runtime descriptor must
  explicitly require capabilities 1; no protocol compatibility is inferred.
- Exports for operations absent from the submitting descriptor, repeated exported
  operations, and uniform names already assigned to another export.
- Invalid GLSL names, names outside the `shaderlod` namespace, reserved double
  underscores, and collisions with existing core/effects/schema fields.

The existing contract constructors additionally validate namespaced operation and
adapter ids, protocol versions, exact revisions, legal work domains, member paths,
digests and actual Iris option keys. Collections are defensively copied.

Several adapters may declare the same exact operation. They reuse its already
registered uniform by passing no new export for that operation. A second name
for an existing operation is rejected. A descriptor can also declare operations
without exporting them; declaration alone supplies no uniform. Empty source
bindings are allowed and cannot select a runtime capability.

## Capability schema and frame behavior

Schema 1 retains `shaderlodCapabilitiesVersion = 1` and the default
`shaderlodVolumeIntegrationAvailable` mapping to the shared volume count
operation. The built-in spatial reference additionally exports
`shaderlodOpaqueSpatialAvailable`; the three capability fields remain separate
from the unchanged 43 effect fields and seven core fields. Additional exports
are additive `uniform1i(PER_FRAME, ...)` booleans.
Their shader consumers must require exact capabilities schema 1 and availability
1, plus their existing core/effect enable, mode, input and quality gates.

Each `CapabilityExport.supplier(frame)` captures its operation once at uniform
binding. Calls read only `EffectUniformFrame.binding()`, shared with all effect
controls for that notifier frame. An unknown operation or any unavailable state
returns 0. Runtime/source/option changes cannot split suppliers within the same
frame; the next notifier callback refreshes the common snapshot. There is no
source hashing, collection construction, or runtime access per uniform call.

## Explicit operation and actual source consumers

Both adapters reuse the existing
[refinement_budget.glsl](../patches/adapters/shared/refinement_budget.glsl)
unchanged. The only effect is the termination count of existing refinements after
an upstream valid-crossing test. Primary 30-iteration search limits, projected
ray geometry, ray increments, sample depth, validity tests, reprojection,
radiance/alpha and sky fallbacks remain upstream. No texture fetch, derivative,
frame selector or late contribution branch was added.

Distance is `length(viewPos)`: camera-relative Euclidean distance in Minecraft
blocks, before traversal mutates the input. Counts are full through 96 blocks;
the requested retention interpolates with `smoothstep(96,192,distance_blocks)`.
Conservative ceiling produces discrete integer changes, which can still pop.
These fixed source distances do not consume advanced mod near/far controls.

[BSL binding](../patches/adapters/bsl-shaders.json):
`world0/world-1/world1/gbuffers_water.fsh` include
`program/gbuffers_water.glsl`, whose fragment path receives
`SHADERLOD_BSL_WATER`. `lib/reflections/simpleReflections.glsl::SimpleReflection`
budgets existing `maxf` before its `Raytrace` call. Original counts are four when
`WATER_NORMALS>0` (the default) and six when `WATER_NORMALS=0`. Minimum is three,
so Fast/Performance can request three/five at full transition; Balanced's 87.5%
retention rounds both back to four/six. `Raytrace` still increments `sr` only
inside `err < lVector` and uses its original `sr >= maxf` test. This minimum-three
candidate is experimental: source inspection proves scope, not acceptable hits.

BSL's simple reflection also serves translucent advanced materials in this same
water program; they use the same crossing semantics and are included in the
candidate's quality obligation. Opaque `roughReflections.glsl` and deferred
programs are untouched. External PBR is not blanket-disabled merely because it
is present. Both ordinary and PBR translucent consumers need runtime inspection.

[Solas binding](../patches/adapters/solas-shader.json): root/Nether/End
`gbuffers_water.fsh` include `programs/gbuffers_water.glsl`, which already defines
`GBUFFERS_WATER`. `lib/pbr/waterReflection.glsl::getReflection` budgets the literal
six-refinement argument with minimum four before its overloaded `Raytrace` call.

The overloaded raytracer forwards that count to `refinedSamples` inside its
original `error < thickness` crossing. External PBR `simpleReflection.glsl` and
raytracer bytes remain unchanged. Colorwheel-specific translucents stay full

# Explicit Iris adapter runtime binding

The mod now separates adapter declarations, exact source eligibility, live Iris
availability, and rendered consumption. Core protocol 2 and effects protocol 2,
their fields, config defaults and commands keep their existing meanings.
An eligible declaration is not evidence that a shader compiled, linked, consumed
the uniform, saved physical work, preserved quality, or improved throughput.

## Registration and frame lifecycle

`EffectUniformsMixin.shaderlod$registerCapabilities` uses the existing pinned
`CommonUniforms.generalCommonUniforms` TAIL seam. It validates a loaded pack once
per actual `ShaderPack` object identity. It does not inject at reload TAIL, use a
pack-name substring, rewrite GLSL, or test pipeline readiness during construction.
The cache holds weak pack identities, including negative source results. A reload
with a new pack object needs a new registration even if its name or bytes match.

`IrisRuntimeAccess` uses Iris 1.8.12 `getCurrentPack()` (an Optional),
`getCurrentPackName()` and `getShaderpacksDirectory()` to locate the selected
source. The display name only locates the container; no name confers support.
Source validation requires both a registered complete source digest and exact
named consumer/helper member digests. ZIPs use SHA-256 of the complete archive
bytes. Folder packs use SHA-256 of sorted UTF-8 rows `member + NUL + memberSHA256
+ LF`. Folder and ZIP identities are separate pins. Paths, duplicate ZIP members,
symlinks, malformed pins and read failures cannot enable an adapter.

Actual option acceptance uses `ShaderPack.getShaderPackOptions()`, its `OptionSet`
and `OptionValues`. Only keys declared in the loaded Boolean/String option maps
are read, including Iris's effective defaults. Queued options, `.txt` contents,
mod configuration and internal program defines do not establish an active key.
Only required keys are examined at a frame boundary; source files are not reread.

Initial capability state is unavailable. The existing `EffectUniformFrame`
notifier listener snapshots effect controls and binding availability together.
All uniform suppliers use that snapshot until the next notifier frame. Live
availability requires the same validated pack identity, `!Iris.isFallback()`,
`IrisApi.isShaderPackInUse()` and accepted effective required options. The pinned
Iris API implementation checks the current non-vanilla pipeline. The binding never
uses `isPackInUseQuick()`. A `currentPack` that survives fallback grants no work
capability. Unknown, absent, unvalidated, conflicting, incompatible or unavailable
bindings supply no operations; the shared shader policy must retain upstream work.

## Capability schema 1

Two additive `uniform1i(PER_FRAME, ...)` registrations are separate from the
existing 43 effects fields:

| Uniform | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `shaderlodCapabilitiesVersion` | 1, the exact capability transport schema |
| `shaderlodVolumeIntegrationAvailable` | 1 only when the validated live adapter declares the shared count operation; otherwise 0 |

`LodOperations.VOLUME_INTEGRATION` is the pack-independent operation key:
`Effect.VOLUMETRICS`, `shaderlod:volume_integration`, `WorkKind.COUNT`.
It does not imply support for other volume operations, rates, or effects.
The shared consumer must require exact schema 1 and availability 1 before applying
a requested budget, in addition to existing core/effect protocol, enable, mode,
input validity and safety gates. Descriptor selection alone is not rendered
consumption proof.

## Exact proposed resource model

OpenGL 4.1 fragment/FBO construction, no compute/images. Two **separate RG32F
atlas texture objects** hold even/odd levels. In each atlas the largest level
occupies the left rectangle; smaller levels stack on its right. Ceil-halving
includes odd edges. Base writes [d,d] from native finite normalized float32
source depth; unknown/nonfinite becomes [0,1]. Explicit four-child min/max
reductions copy endpoints without averaging. Each reduction samples the other
texture object using integer texelFetch level 0 while writing its own rectangle.
No same-texture framebuffer feedback; no ordinary generateMipmap. No clear of
previously written level rectangles during construction. Consumers need two
additional sampler groups, explicit integer fetch and parity selection.

| Domain extent | Draws/frame | Both atlas storage | Nominal minimum traffic/frame |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1920 × 1200 | 12 | 28,800,000 bytes | 58,368,904 bytes |
| 2560 × 1440 | 13 | 46,080,000 bytes | 93,389,496 bytes |
| 480 × 300 native quarter domain | 10 | 1,800,000 bytes | 3,648,904 bytes |

Traffic includes base depth read, every existing child once per reduction, and
all RG32F writes. Four fetch expressions at odd boundaries can cost more; FBO
transitions, atlas padding/initialization, consumer queries, fallback and
retained native resources are additional. This is nominal traffic, not measured
external-memory bandwidth or GPU time. Two independent depth domains double
these amounts; no shared MC/DH nonlinear raw min operation is valid.

## Producer order and correctness boundary

Reused pinned Iris bytecode in the receipt shows beginTranslucents **copies
pre-translucent depth before deferredRenderer.renderAll**. Thus deferred opaque
construction could precede later forward water; forward water does not itself
make reuse impossible. Fresh `javap -p -c` of exact Iris MixinLevelRenderer/HandRenderer/RenderTargets
now verifies `beginHand → renderSolid → beginTranslucents`; beginHand copies

Thus ordinary deferred opaque depth includes the solid hand, while no-hand
