# Per-effect work policy

The dependency-free `com.pp.shaderlod.lod` model describes requested work caps for
explicit shader adapters. It does not register Iris uniforms, read NeoForge config,
patch GLSL, or establish shader consumption. The new general LOD goal uses Photon
as its reference consumer; another pack would need an independently reviewed
adapter and its own runtime evidence.

## Immutable model

`EffectPolicy(enabled, preserveSalientLighting, bands, mediumWorkRatio,
farWorkRatio)` snapshots one override. `DistanceBands(nearBlocks, farBlocks,
transitionBlocks)` uses camera-relative Euclidean distance in Minecraft block
units. Transition width is the **full** width centered on each boundary, matching
the existing core contract: 32/96/8 means transitions at 28–36 and 92–100 blocks.
Smoothstep blends retained work from 1 to the medium ratio, then to the far ratio.
Zero width changes tiers exactly at the boundary. Bands cannot overlap or extend
below zero, and endpoint arithmetic must remain finite.

Ratios satisfy `0 <= farWorkRatio <= mediumWorkRatio <= 1`. They cap the fraction
of an adapter's actual upstream work count; they are not universal sample counts,
effect strength, radius, shader quality preset, or screen resolution. Constructor
validation rejects malformed configuration. Runtime decisions preserve original
work for global disable, effect disable, protected lighting, invalid/null effect,
non-finite/negative distance, negative work count, or an invalid retained floor.

The protection flag is part of the immutable policy. With it enabled, shadow
filtering and ambient occlusion keep their upstream budgets even if smaller ratios
were configured. Other effects still need their own quality review: the flag does
not imply that all reflection, water, volumetric or material reductions are safe.

| Effect | Stable uniform key suffix | Default block bands | Protected lighting |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shadow filtering | `ShadowFiltering` | 32 / 96 / 8 | Yes |
| Ambient occlusion | `AmbientOcclusion` | 32 / 96 / 8 | Yes |
| Reflections | `Reflections` | 32 / 96 / 8 | No |
| Volumetrics | `Volumetrics` | 32 / 96 / 8 | No |
| Water surface | `WaterSurface` | 96 / 256 / 32 | No |
| Materials | `Materials` | 32 / 96 / 8 | No |

Do not serialize enum ordinals. These suffixes are stable identifiers; an adapter
must document which operations each broad effect category actually covers.
Volumetrics does not imply every fog/cloud operation shares the same useful bands
or even has a valid surface-distance input.

`defaultsFor(effect)` disables the new override, sets both ratios to 1, and enables
lighting protection. 32/96 are project starting points, not measured optima; water
96/256/32 comes from existing Photon water bands. Unity/off defaults reflect the
current evidence: the recent five-effect pilot regressed, lower shadow/AO budgets
lost salient distant structure, and a far reflection skip produced a visible water
band. No new quality reduction is promoted by this API. See
[STATUS](STATUS.md), [DECISIONS](DECISIONS.md), and the
[Photon glint audit](PHOTON_GLINT_SOURCE_AUDIT.md).

## Explicit adapter use

```java
var policy = new EffectPolicy(true, true, new DistanceBands(32, 96, 8), 0.5, 0.25);
var budget = policy.decide(globalEnabled, Effect.REFLECTIONS,
        cameraRelativeDistanceBlocks, upstreamTraceSteps, minimumLegalTraceSteps);
int requestedTraceSteps = budget.workLimit();
```

This example requests a reduction; it is not a recommended Photon preset. The
adapter supplies the actual upstream count from the selected pack options and
feature path. It also supplies the legal retained floor: zero permits skipping
all work; one preserves at least one iteration. A zero upstream budget remains
zero. Invalid upstream counts are returned unchanged so the caller retains its
original path rather than inventing a valid-looking reduced budget.

Quantization uses `ceil(upstream * retainedRatio)` and clamps to the legal floor
and upstream count. Apart from the declared floor, rounding retains less than one
additional work item above the continuous requested count. A cap cannot increase
the upstream count, including `Integer.MAX_VALUE`. `WorkBudget.retentionRatio`
reports the continuous request; `workLimit` is the integer result after rounding
and the floor. `reason` describes policy eligibility, and `reduced()` reports only
that the requested integer limit shrank. Neither proves fewer physical GPU
operations.

Shader ports must reproduce smoothstep, finite-input guards, non-overlap, protected
lighting, upward integer rounding and bounded caps. Drivers generally evaluate
GLSL floats with lower precision than Java doubles; transport must validate its
float range and use source fixtures plus actual driver/readback checks. This Java
model is an oracle for intended policy, not proof of bit-exact GLSL execution.
An adapter that changes loop counts must also preserve its integration interval,
normalization, upstream early-exit rules and any minimum legal refinement work.
It must not replace semantic work solely because an effect enum exists.

Exact work reuse is a separate capability. Reusing an identical texel/depth fetch
while preserving original iteration positions and evaluation math can remain
eligible when shadow/AO budgets are protected or ratios are 1. The work-cap model
neither enables nor forbids that independent adapter optimization. For example,
duplicate AO taps can share an identical depth fetch but cannot skip horizon math
that still depends on the original fractional ray position.

## Registered additive extension: source state

The integration source now registers a separate NeoForge client config and Iris
uniform extension. `ShaderLod.java` registers `ShaderLodEffectConfig.SPEC` in
`shaderlod-effects-client.toml`. Its six `effects.<effect>` sections use enum names
in lower snake case: `shadow_filtering`, `ambient_occlusion`, `reflections`,
`volumetrics`, `water_surface`, and `materials`. Each section exposes `mode`,
`near`, `far`, `transition`, `mediumWorkRatio`, `farWorkRatio`, and
`preserveSalientLighting`. Defaults are INHERIT, the table's block bands, unity
ratios and lighting protection enabled.

The config spec bounds near to 1–4095 and far to 2–4096; snapshot conversion
then raises far to at least near+1. Transition's config range is
0–512; conversion additionally caps it to `min(near*2, far-near)`. Far ratio is
capped to medium ratio. These are deterministic normalization rules in the config
integration, while direct construction of the pure API still rejects malformed
input. The pure API supports finite positive distances beyond those config ranges.
Snapshot construction itself does not catch invalid/non-finite raw config values;
the config spec is responsible for validating persisted entries. Do not infer a
transport exception recovery path from the numerical API's invalid-runtime guards.

For shadow/AO with protection enabled, the config snapshot publishes both ratios
as 1 while retaining the immutable policy protection flag. Protection is therefore
baked into the transmitted ratios; there is no separate protection uniform. This
protects quality budget counts and does not disable independent exact work reuse.

`EffectUniformsMixin`, listed in `shaderlod.mixins.json`, injects at the tail of
pinned Iris `CommonUniforms.generalCommonUniforms`. It registers 37 PER_FRAME
fields: one integer `shaderlodEffectsVersion` with value 1, plus these six fields
for each `shaderlod<Suffix>` prefix in the effect table above:

| Field suffix | Iris registration | Source value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Mode` | Integer | Explicit mode protocol value 0/1/2 |
| `Near` | Float from double supplier | Validated `nearBlocks` |
| `Far` | Float from double supplier | Validated `farBlocks` |
| `Transition` | Float from double supplier | Validated full `transitionBlocks` width |
| `MediumWorkRatio` | Float from double supplier | Validated/protected medium retained ratio |
| `FarWorkRatio` | Float from double supplier | Validated/protected far retained ratio |

For example, the exact AO names are `shaderlodAmbientOcclusionMode`,
`shaderlodAmbientOcclusionNear`, `shaderlodAmbientOcclusionFar`,
`shaderlodAmbientOcclusionTransition`, `shaderlodAmbientOcclusionMediumWorkRatio`,
and `shaderlodAmbientOcclusionFarWorkRatio`. Enum ordinals are not used for modes.
The existing seven core fields, including `shaderlodBridgeVersion=2` and global
`shaderlodEnabled`, retain their existing registration and semantics.

An `EffectUniformFrame` instance belongs to each registration group. Its frame
notifier callback clears cached controls; the first queried per-effect supplier
lazily takes one immutable map snapshot, and subsequent suppliers in that group
reuse it for the frame. Registration of the constant extension version alone does
not query the config. This is source-level supplier behavior, not a measured
overhead reduction or proof that a particular program linked these uniforms.

No Photon adapter consumption, driver linking/readback, config reload behavior,
runtime mixin application or performance gain has been established by this source
review. Build acceptance and the GPU/runtime owner must record those checks
separately.

| Mode | Intended adapter behavior |
| --- | --- |
| 0: INHERIT | Keep existing adapter/core policy; additive defaults use this mode. |
| 1: FULL | Retain the pack's original work for this effect. |
| 2: ADAPTIVE | Apply the validated custom policy when global enable and protection permit. |

`EffectPolicy.enabled=false` means retain original work at the numerical layer;
it does **not** mean INHERIT. Resolve mode before invoking the custom numerical
model. Global disable selects the original pack work even when a per-effect mode
is INHERIT. Unknown protocol versions/modes, unsupported pinned pack revisions,
absent mod, missing transport, or invalid converted fields must select the
original pack path. A declared effect name is not evidence that any path consumes
its ratios, and missing capability must not silently become a partial override.

Record adapter declarations separately from actual consumption:

| Adapter declaration | Consumption evidence required before acceptance |
| --- | --- |
| Pinned pack revision/source and maintained patch hashes | Selected archive and linked program/source identity |
| Protocol version, supported fields and effect/suboperation mapping | Driver link/readback of those exact fields |
| Distance source/units, upstream count source, legal floor and quantization | Original/off/on in-world behavior and config/reload checks |
| Quality cap versus exact reuse capability, lighting guard behavior | Relevant loop/fetch/work evidence and protected/full-path controls |
| DH paths supported or unsupported | Actual DH-present/absent rendering and boundary checks |

Keep this as an explicit adapter contract; no automatic GLSL rewriting or
capability registry is introduced. The next integration should consume one
measured effect in pinned Photon sources, retain original/mod-absent and disabled
controls, and report compilation, work avoidance, repeated GPU/total-frame timing,
and transition/motion quality separately.

# Rendering bottleneck options

Audit checkpoint: 2026-10-04. Scope is pinned Photon v1.3b, Iris 1.8.12,
Sodium 0.6.13, DH 3.3.3, Minecraft 1.21.1, and the current Apple M3 Max
profile. This is source/bytecode inspection and a proposal for bounded tests;
new optimizations and performance claims require the coordinator's measurements.
No shader/renderer source was changed for this audit.

## What the current evidence supports

The previous serial measurements found real reductions in cloud, fog, AO and
lighting passes but only 1–5.5% in the whole GameRenderer GPU timeline interval.
The pass-profile OFF means were clouds 0.539ms, fog 0.164ms, AO 0.057ms,
and deferred lighting 0.358ms. These came from alternating query frames and
cannot be summed into an exact single-frame decomposition. As a rough planning
ceiling, their approximately 1.1ms budget is small against the 8–9ms render
interval. Eliminating AO entirely trades tree depth for roughly hundredths of a
millisecond. The user rejected that tradeoff.

A mechanism saving half of its own work must cover about 30% of a frame to save
15% overall, before extra overhead. A 20% mechanism needs roughly 75% coverage
for that target. Find a large enough measured fraction before another round of
sample caps. GPU elapsed intervals also include command-starvation/scheduling
intervals; unaccounted time is not evidence of GPU busy overhead. CPU wall and
thread time, GPU draw scopes, and pass scopes must be interpreted together.

Current inactive Mac features include environment/sky reflections, colored
lighting, colored shadows, variable penumbra shadows, and cloud shadows. More
SSR/POM/LPV caps cannot explain the current frame. Their successful compilation
is not a measured contributor. Record every high/lower/adaptive option and the
same sampler-safe feature mask; do not call a masked profile full Photon Ultra.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

Photon's existing TAAU lowers linear raster scale; 0.75 means approximately

The source uses `taau_render_scale` across geometry and fullscreen programs;
actual Iris/DH viewport behavior still needs driver validation.

The current cloud pass is already quarter linear resolution (1/16 pixel area),
AO and fog use half linear buffer sizes, and sky-map output is only 192×108.
A lower-resolution cloud or fog prototype alone has a modest ceiling in the

## Larger mechanisms, gated on attribution

### 1. Distance-aware geometry transition into DH

If measured Sodium opaque/cutout raster or submission dominates, first test a
plain shorter vanilla radius with the same warmed DH reach. This establishes
what existing coarse geometry can save. Rendering vanilla 24 chunks while DH
also supplies coarse scenery needlessly preserves detailed distant meshes if
that extra precision is no longer visible. The simple lower-radius setting is
a required control, not itself a new ShaderLOD implementation.

An adaptive prototype could retain full vanilla geometry near the camera and
reduce outer detailed rings in favor of DH, with a stable overlap/fade interval
and enough hysteresis to avoid rebuilding on every frame. Do not discard random
sections or skip cutout draws: that loses tree silhouettes, causes holes, and
invalidates lighting. Do not shorten the independent shadow-caster coverage just
because visible terrain changes; inspect distant casts and water boundaries.

Audited seams:

- `SodiumWorldRenderer.setupTerrain(Camera, Viewport, boolean, boolean)` prepares
  visibility; `drawChunkLayer(RenderType, ChunkRenderMatrices, double, double,
  double)` submits a terrain layer.
- `DefaultChunkRenderer.render(...)` walks region render lists,
  `fillCommandBuffer(...)` emits draw commands, and `executeDrawBatch(...)` uses
  `DrawCommandList.multiDrawElementsBaseVertex`. Sodium already batches draws;
  replacing it with per-section calls is not an optimization.
- `RenderBufferHandler.buildRenderList(RenderParams)` builds DH visibility and
  exposes visible/culled counts through its debug strings.
- `LodQuadTree.calcExpectedDetailLevel(...)`, `calcDetailLevelFromDistance(...)`,
  and `updateDetailLevelVariables()` control selection with
  `detailDropOffDistanceUnit` / `detailDropOffLogBase` and leaf detail limits.
- `LodRenderer.render(...)`, `renderDeferred(...)`, and private
  `renderTerrain(...)` separate DH phases. The concrete
  `GlDhTerrainRenderer.render(...)` delegates to its terrain shader program.

Prefer bounded DH quality/config changes through its audited API before a new
mesh renderer. Changing horizontal/vertical quality triggers background data or
mesh work; exclude that rebuild/upload period and keep both configurations warm.
Current `maxHorizontalResolution=BLOCK`, `horizontalQuality=MEDIUM`,
`verticalQuality=MEDIUM`, `transparency=COMPLETE`, and
`vanillaFadeMode=DOUBLE_PASS` are useful controls. A SINGLE_PASS fade comparison
is a separate quality tradeoff and matters only if the fade stages actually cost
appreciable time under Iris. Retain overdraw prevention; don't render overlapping
vanilla/DH opaque layers merely to create an expensive baseline.

### 2. Depth-aware low-resolution lighting, keeping occlusion/shadows

If deferred fragment shading becomes large at a genuinely detailed supported
preset, move costly lighting into a reduced-resolution output and reconstruct
with depth, normal, and material guards. Keep near geometry and disocclusions at
full quality. A comparison to original Photon TAAU and simple lower lighting
quality determines whether selective reconstruction is worth its complexity.

Exact Photon seams are `d4_deferred_shading.fsh` for the final opaque lighting,
`d3_ao.fsh` for half-resolution AO/history, and `d4_deferred_shading.fsh`'s
existing depth-weighted four-neighbor AO reconstruction. The latter demonstrates
how combined-depth inverse projection is used across vanilla and DH. A new
lighting target/pipeline needs explicit buffer ownership, format, viewport,
coordinate changes, and consumer declarations; it is not a safe numeric option
change. Iris supports per-pass viewport scaling through
`CompositeRenderer.Pass.viewportScale`; `renderAll()` binds a pass's framebuffer
and viewport before the fullscreen draw.

Fog currently uses `smooth_filter` in `c1_blend_layers.fsh`, not a depth-aware
reconstruction. Adding a quarter-resolution fog buffer without a bilateral
upsampler risks haloing foreground silhouettes. Fog/AO share half-resolution
colortex6/7/14 at different stages, so shrinking those buffers blindly changes
multiple effects and can break history/depth correspondence. The output change
must preserve each stage's exact interpretation. Additional sampler bindings
may exceed the Mac's budget; do not silently remove lighting to make room.

This mechanism can retain low-frequency AO and shadow structure rather than
returning neutral far AO. However, current AO is too small to justify a special
renderer alone. Continue treating AO bypass as a diagnostic, not a default.

### 3. Temporal reuse of sky/cloud/fog work

The sky-map texture is cached *for sampling* by reflections and lighting, but
Photon's `d0_sky_map.fsh`/`.vsh` contain no periodic update gate. Iris
`CompositeRenderer.renderAll()` iterates and draws the configured pass every
frame. A zero median elapsed query does not prove refresh skipping. The map
includes special lighting-color texels at x=191, and it uses a fixed sea-level
cloud origin rather than the rendered camera altitude.

A bounded refresh prototype must keep light/ambient palette texels current and
refresh cloud-bearing map texels less often, with explicit invalidation for
shader reload, dimension, sun/weather discontinuity, lightning and changed
quality. Preserve the existing texture contents on skipped cloud updates;
`discard` alone is unsafe if the target is cleared or ping-pong-swapped. Iris
buffer-flip and clear directives need audit before implementing reuse. This is
an explicit temporal approximation, not distance LOD, and stale reflections/
lighting must be tested under motion and storms.

`d1_clouds.fsh` and `d2_clouds_upscaling.fsh` already implement temporal
reprojection/upscaling, with colortex9/10 low-res buffers and cloud history in
colortex11/12. Lower refresh rate or checkerboard work can reuse that machinery
only with valid reprojection, disocclusion rejection, and camera-cut invalidation.
Prove the cloud fraction is large first; lowering refresh of a 0.4ms pass cannot
produce a 15% improvement in an 8ms frame by itself.

### 4. CPU submission and immutable state

Pinned Iris `ProgramUniforms.update()` evaluates PER_FRAME uniforms once per
program/frame. `IntUniform.updateValue()` compares a cached value before calling
`glUniform1i`. Floats use the same style of value caching. Constant ShaderLOD
values are therefore not necessarily uploaded every draw, despite their
PER_FRAME registration.

ShaderLOD currently calls `ShaderLodConfig.snapshot()` separately for several
suppliers; each computes cross-field bounds and constructs a record. Cache an
immutable sanitized snapshot on config/control change, or once per frame,
if CPU measurements show meaningful cost. This is a bounded cleanup, with no
reason yet to expect millisecond gains. A hypothetical “remove uniform upload”
rewrite would duplicate functionality Iris already provides.

Iris `CompositeRenderer.renderAll()` also updates programs, custom uniforms,
samplers/images, mipmaps and framebuffer/viewport state, and clears active
program/sampler state after the stage. Measure relevant CPU methods before
removing state transitions. Some state invalidation protects integration with
Minecraft, Sodium and DH; deleting it speculatively can corrupt later passes.

## Dynamic loops and the disabled comparison

A uniform quality decision can stop a loop early while still making its bound
nonconstant to the driver. This may inhibit unrolling, change register pressure
or instruction scheduling, even in the disabled mode. GLSL compilation does not
expose Apple ISA/occupancy and does not prove this explanation. Nearby distance
zones are usually spatially coherent except their transition bands; do not blame
warp divergence solely because branches exist.

The diagnostic sequence should use the same upstream common quality:

1. Original Photon high.
2. Patched Photon with live bridge OFF.
3. Patched Photon with bridge disabled and LOD compile-time disabled.
4. Patched adaptive with important occlusion/shadow structure retained.
5. Original lower quality as a separate practical control.

If (2) regresses and (3) recovers, investigate branch/unrolling overhead with a
single affected pass. If all three are close, do not spend days specializing
loop shaders. A prototype using constant maximum loops plus uniform early
breaks may compile differently but still needs measured evidence. Static shader
quality variants can recover specialization at the cost of reloads/variant
management; do not introduce a universal rewriter or claim continuous adaptation
when switching programs requires shader reload.

## Acceptance for a prototype

Implement only after attribution identifies a fraction large enough for the
proof target. Report original high, original lower, patched disabled, and
adaptive results with repeated warmed serial blocks, matched timings overhead,
GPU render and CPU metrics, sample counts and variability. Include movement,
TAA stability, near silhouettes, far tree depth/shadows, vanilla/DH seam, water
and disocclusions. A 15% saving achieved by a simple existing lower preset with
better fidelity than adaptive is evidence to prefer that preset, not to claim
success for new distance LOD infrastructure.

Source evidence is the hash-locked local Photon ZIP and exact runtime jars in
`dev/runtime.lock.json`; methods above were verified with `javap -p -c` against
those jars. Runtime support and which renderer implementation is active belong
to the measured client, not this read-only audit.

## CPU-attributed geometry prototype proposal

The coordinator's forest attribution now shows approximately 7.83ms runTick
thread CPU within an 8.93ms frame wall interval, GameRenderer 7.36ms thread CPU,
vanilla opaque/cutout submission 1.85ms, translucency 0.29ms, terrain setup
0.40ms, and DH opaque/translucent submission 0.44/0.54ms. This supports a CPU
submission hypothesis and a bounded geometry control. It does not prove that
reducing radius 24→16 will save a particular fraction, or that a GPU interval
can be subtracted from CPU time. Report final measurements in the results doc.

### Opt-in detailed-terrain cap with DH preserving long reach

Prototype configuration: `geometry.enabled=false` by default and
`geometry.vanillaChunkCap=16` (minimum 8); users retain their normal render
setting. Scope initially includes the supported Photon/DH combination in a
loaded world. Keep shader sample LOD separate so an ablation can enable geometry
without aggressive far AO or shadow cuts. The geometry policy need not require
the patched pack when the original pinned Photon also supports DH; it must
require ShaderLOD's main enable flag and explicit geometry opt-in. The original
baseline with ShaderLOD absent receives no cap.

Recommended seam is a return-value cap on
`Options.getEffectiveRenderDistance()`: return `min(originalReturn, cap)` while
the latched policy is active, otherwise return the original value. Do not write
`Options.renderDistance().set(...)`, persist a replacement user preference, or
broadcast a lower server distance. The raw option and `options.txt` stay intact,
and the server-imposed minimum already present in the original return survives.
The HUD/config should display both requested and effective radius. User edits
remain authoritative: values below the cap remain below it; increasing the
requested value changes only the remembered/manual preference while the cap is
active. Turning geometry/mod/DH off immediately recovers the current preference,
not a stale value captured before the user edited it.

This common getter is deliberate. Pinned Sodium
`SodiumWorldRenderer.setupTerrain` compares it to the stored renderer radius and
calls `reload()` when it changes; `reload()` constructs a new
`RenderSectionManager` using that radius. Pinned DH's NeoForge
`MinecraftRenderWrapper_neoforge.getRenderDistance()` also calls the same
getter, so overdraw/fade can follow the new vanilla boundary. A Sodium-only
radius override with DH still believing vanilla is 24 can leave a missing
16–24-chunk ring. Changing the getter also affects fog/entity-view scale and
other vanilla consumers; document that consequence rather than presenting this
as a pure batching optimization. Shadow caster coverage and actual DH overlap
must be validated, not assumed.

Change the effective cap only at explicit policy/lifecycle transitions, not from
instantaneous FPS every frame. Radius changes destroy/rebuild Sodium renderer
state. At initial enable and disable, suspend benchmark sampling until section
rebuild/upload and DH overlap settle. Do not choose a fluctuating radius while
measuring the static kill test.

### DH readiness, optional dependency, and fail-open behavior

Public pinned APIs give useful readiness checks:

- Test NeoForge mod presence before loading the optional DH adapter class.
  Public `DhApi.Delayed.configs`/`worldProxy`/`renderProxy` may initially be null.
- Require `worldProxy.worldLoaded()` and
  `configs.graphics().renderingEnabled().getValue()` true. Check the current
  world/dimension identity separately; a loaded DH world alone does not identify
  the same active dimension.
- `IrisApi.getInstance().isShaderPackInUse()` confirms shaders are active but
  does **not** confirm DH compatibility. Pinned internal
  `Iris.getPipelineManager().getPipelineNullable()` can be checked for
  `IrisRenderingPipeline`, with `getDHTerrainShader().isPresent()` and
  `getDHCompat().getInstance() != null`. Evaluate at a safe client/render
  lifecycle boundary, never while recursively computing render distance.
- A DH `DhApiBeforeRenderEvent` listener can latch successful rendering for the
  current world; guard `IrisApi.isRenderingShadowPass()` because the render-pass
  enum describes opaque/transparency rather than an explicit shadow pass.
  `getDhDepthTextureGlId()` returns `DhApiResult<Integer>` with `success` and
  `payload`; a valid positive texture can corroborate initialized GL rendering.
  It does not prove that the nearer replacement ring has complete cached meshes.

Do **not** call `DHCompat.hasRenderingEnabled()`/`checkFrame()` from an Options
getter. The audited bytecode can trigger an Iris pipeline reload when DH config
or GUI scale changes. That turns a nominal getter into a reentrant renderer
mutation. Compute a small immutable readiness/policy state once at an appropriate
client boundary and let the getter perform only a cheap boolean/minimum check.

Start fail-open: original radius until DH readiness is established. Clear
readiness immediately on world unload, dimension change, shader reload/failure,
DH disable or policy disable. API linkage/initialization failures disable only
the geometry policy and expose the reason; they do not crash optional-DH users.
Avoid rapid cap on/off if initial uploads are temporarily late. The first
production prototype should be a fixed opt-in cap in a warmed DH-supported world,
with honest cache-coverage limitations, not an automatic claim that distant
terrain can always replace all unloaded detailed chunks. Test a cold DH cache
and absent generation: fall back rather than show missing terrain.

### Coarser DH as a separate control

Keep `lodChunkRenderDistanceRadius=128` and first compare
`horizontalQuality=MEDIUM`/`LOW` with the same vertical quality and cache coverage.
DH's public `graphics().horizontalQuality()` returns an
`IDhApiConfigValue<EDhApiHorizontalQuality>` supporting `getTrueValue()` (user
value), `getApiValue()`, `setValue(...)`, and `clearValue()`. A later production
override can use that API, but restoring/clearing another mod's override is not
safe. Only clear an override this policy demonstrably owns; respect concurrent
manual/API changes. Do not include an unmeasured automatic DH quality override
in the first vanilla-cap prototype. It complicates both ownership and the
quality attribution.

### A CPU-only backend alternative preserving geometry

Sodium already uses `MultiDrawBatch` and `multiDrawElementsBaseVertex` per render
region. The concrete potential seam is caching opaque `fillCommandBuffer(...)`
results while visibility, section mesh allocations and camera-dependent face
selection remain unchanged. Still update region model matrices and submit all
the same triangles. First instrument `fillCommandBuffer`,
`setModelMatrixUniforms`, and `executeDrawBatch` separately: a 1.85ms whole-layer
CPU interval does not identify command assembly as its dominant portion.

This is not a trivial flag. `SectionRenderDataStorage` has no public content
revision: vertex/index setters/removers, buffer resize and delete can invalidate
stored draw pointers. `ChunkRenderList` is reset/sorted/filled and tracks visible
frames, not a stable membership revision. A correct cache therefore needs
explicit invalidation for those mutations, visibility membership, camera-cell
face changes, region disposal and renderer/shader reload. Translucent sorting
requires additional invalidation and should remain upstream in a first test.
Never cache raw pointers across buffer relocation without generation tracking.
If the isolated assembly cost is small, stop this approach; inventing a second
chunk renderer or disabling geometry to improve a batching benchmark would not
be the same mechanism.

Acceptance for the fixed-cap kill test: compare original 24/DH128, original
16/DH128 as the simple existing-setting control, and ShaderLOD's requested24 /
effective16 / DH128 policy. Keep original lighting/occlusion options, report
world submission/thread costs plus complete frame/GPU metrics, and inspect the
vanilla/DH boundary, tree silhouettes, water and shadows. The policy should
match the practical lower-radius control; any incremental claim must explain
what it actually adds beyond making that existing tradeoff explicit/reversible.

# Core render-frame history transport

2026-10-06. Bounded implementation for the proven live-pixel cloud-history
rectangle mismatch. This adds transport, not a shader consumer or an accepted
quality repair. Root retains build integration, client and GPU ownership.

`CoreUniformFrame` holds one immutable seven-field core snapshot per Iris frame
notifier. `CommonUniformsMixin` registers all existing core suppliers against that
snapshot. Core protocol 2, names, preset ordinals, distances and enabled/debug
values retain their meanings. No effect transport, config, runtime binding,
adapter source or pass graph was modified.

Two additive integer uniforms form temporal protocol 1:

| Uniform | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `shaderlodTemporalVersion` | 1 only after a valid notifier callback with a known world and core snapshot; 0 before the first callback or when state is unavailable. |
| `shaderlodHistoryReset` | 1 on first valid frame, any core change (including both enabled directions), world object change, new notifier/reload, frame discontinuity, invalid state and recovery. Otherwise 0. |

Suppliers only read the frame value. They never advance or consume a reset.
Repeated notifications with the same Iris render counter cannot split a frame.
World identity uses the actual Minecraft level object, deferred until a notifier
callback; dimension-name equality does not establish the same world. Unknown
world or a runtime snapshot exception retains coherent core values and advertises
temporal version 0/reset 1. Initial config sampling preserves the old registration
requirement that config be available; it does not read Minecraft or frame state.

## Pinned lifecycle evidence

Actual local Iris NeoForge `1.8.12+mc1.21.1` JAR SHA-256:
`3e3f94d2d5cdcb8145c4385d521974aa2d8669b2cc212351f70cf06488182e83`.
The repository requires Iris `[1.8.12,1.8.13)`; this proof is not extrapolated to
another Iris patch line.

JDK 21 `javap -p -c`, plus verbose annotation inspection, establishes:

- `MixinGameRenderer.iris$startFrame` is injected at `render` HEAD and increments
  `SystemTimeUniforms.COUNTER` before level rendering. This is a render counter,
  not a client tick or a uniform invocation count.
- `MixinLevelRenderer.iris$beginLevelRender` invokes `beginLevelRendering` after
  `RenderSystem.clear` in `renderLevel`, before normal world shader draws.
- `IrisRenderingPipeline` constructs one new `FrameUpdateNotifier` per pipeline.
  `beginLevelRendering` invokes `onNewFrame` once at bytecode offset 449, before
  custom-uniform update (456) and begin-pass rendering.
- `FrameUpdateNotifier` iterates its listener ArrayList synchronously in
  registration order. The core listener is registered once per notifier.
- `ProgramUniforms.update` uses the same SystemTime render counter for its
  per-frame supplier stage. The frame state has already been captured when these
  rendering suppliers run.

The Iris counter wraps at 720,720 and resets on lifecycle changes. Discontinuity
conservatively requests a reset, including the wrap. A pipeline not rendered on
the immediately preceding frame also resets when resumed. This implementation
does not claim support for rendering different world objects through the same
notifier in one GameRenderer frame; the first callback remains the coherent
snapshot for that frame. Such a renderer would need a separately audited seam.

## Consumer and common policy

[Shared helper](../shaderpacks/common/shaders/include/shaderlod/projected_material_budget.glsl)
is uniform-free. It consumes the existing work policy, radial distance in
Minecraft blocks, full [0,1] relief ray in local tile UV, UV-per-raster-pixel
Jacobian columns, base-level tile size in texels, and output-pixels-per-raster-pixel
scale. Full ray is never inferred from material alpha extrema. Photon can later
supply its existing gradient/tile transform and `POM_DEPTH*(1-fade)` ray through
one explicit hook; its march/preceding-position semantics still need its own
small consumer patch. No Photon consumer is implemented here.

With local-tile Jacobian G and whole-depth ray R, the guard computes
`length(inverse(G)*R)` raster pixels, scales to output pixels, and computes
`length(R*tileSize)` base-level texels. The retained count is at least half the
selected count, at least `ceil(pixelTravel/0.25)`, and at least
`ceil(texelTravel/0.5)`. Ill-conditioned/singular Jacobians, nonfinite inputs,
invalid units/scale, invalid work/transport or invalid policy retain full work.
The inverse is an explicit 2x2 expression; there are no extra texture reads,
samplers, passes, mip generation, caches or classifiers. Projection runs before
the primary march and only after cheap full-work protection has passed.

This bounds nominal depth-step spacing under a local tangent-plane estimate.
It does **not** bound total relief below0.5pixel, establish the same first height
intersection, or prove a numerical lighting/shadow error bound. A narrow ridge
can fall between coarse samples. Atlas discontinuities, quad boundaries,
perspective and interpolation remain approximation limits despite conditioning
checks. Altered UV/depth can change normal/specular/albedo, slope and self-shadow
outputs even though all consuming equations remain original.

For optimization iteration use the maintained standard test, on the authorized machine with a prepared managed client slot and authentic original pack and options:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test \
  --profile /path/to/prepared/client \
  --pack /path/to/original-pack.zip \
```

On Linux ARM64 use `python3 scripts/linux_arm64_runtime.py benchmark test` with the same arguments. Select an existing loader/version/scene slot; keep the report outside that slot and on the same filesystem as the profile. Confirm the lane is free and the inputs match the intended tuple before launch. Do not reset a slot owned by a client or interrupted operation. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py checkout --help` describes managed checkout. Use `run_storage.copytree` for profile/world copies; it enforces storage limits.

The standard test targets the prepared NeoForge 1.21.1 benchmark protocol. A valid slower result is still a result; a failed or invalid run is not a speed conclusion. Inspect `summary.json`, errors and restoration before proceeding. A short result is not proof of visual equivalence, DH/PBR compatibility or final closure. Compare matched total-frame measurements and disclose drift and scope.

G01 MakeUp copy elimination and G02 BSL mip elimination also collect existing untimed work witnesses after each measurement, disarming them before further timing. The BSL witness requires a separate untimed reload; inspect its completeness rather than inferring execution from parsed directives. # Repeated serial benchmark protocol

The proof runner records independent JVM launches, uses interleaved condition
ordering and retains failures. The coordinator exclusively owns the GPU and must
close preview clients first. This tooling does not establish any new performance
result by itself.

## Inputs and controls

Prepare isolated profiles using the coordinator's proof-profile preparation
script under `run-workloads/photon-proof/`. Each scene contains `high`,
`patched-off`, and `adaptive` profiles. Original `high` has no ShaderLOD mod;
`patched-off` loads the patched pack and mod with its live config disabled;
`adaptive` enables distance logic. Include the simpler `lower` quality control
where appropriate. Shared `control.json` must not override `enabled` or terrain
settings when testing shader-only benefits. All profiles must derive from the
same warmed source save and carry `workload-manifest.json` provenance.

Iris requires Sodium on this target. `minimal` therefore means Iris/Sodium plus
required runtime components, without additional optional optimizers. `optimized`
adds the coordinator's pinned optional mod stack. The runner passes
`-PperformanceStack=minimal/optimized` and `-PincludeDh=true/false` to Gradle.
Actual loaded mod IDs/versions and profile mod-jar SHA-256 hashes are captured;
request labels alone are not evidence that a stack loaded successfully.

Before the first launch, the runner hashes archives, shader options, camera
control, scene provenance, and relevant config files. It verifies stable shader,
camera and source identity again before each repeat. Minecraft legitimately
rewrites `options.txt` at shutdown, so its hash is recorded but not treated as an
immutable subsequent-launch input. Iris also rewrites pack option files with a
timestamp and removes explicit default values. Raw option-file bytes are retained
as evidence but are **not** compared with prelaunch bytes. The runner parses pack
source defaults to normalize requested input files, then validates every requested
active option against Iris's loaded effective values. Unrecognized requests fail;
only an unchanged upstream `INFO` default can be absent, because that profile
information selector is not asserted to control performance.

The runtime reads `Iris.getCurrentPack().get().getShaderPackOptions()`, enumerates
`getOptionSet().getBooleanOptions()/getStringOptions()`, and resolves values with
`getOptionValues().getBooleanValueOrDefault(name)/getStringValueOrDefault(name)`.
It records the sorted complete effective map and canonical JSON SHA-256 at both
measurement boundaries. These APIs were inspected in the pinned Iris jar.
Effective values must stay identical throughout capture and across repeat
launches for the same condition. Paired quality comparison uses these loaded
values, including defaults, instead of incomplete normalized option-file text.
Actual framebuffer, requested/effective
radius, camera, day/weather, enabled/preset state and Iris pipeline state are
captured at both measurement boundaries. Changed inputs, disabled shaders,
fallback, wrong pack or wrong LOD state invalidate the run. Source-save hashes
are preparation provenance; they do not assert byte-for-byte equality of mutable
save files after Minecraft has written them.

A per-run UUID in `workload-request.json` must match the fresh report. Prior
reports move into the output directory; an old report cannot satisfy a new run.
The runner checks process exclusion, waits for the complete Gradle/JVM exit,
rejects fatal shader/control/write error markers, and preserves invalid fresh
reports. On timeout it terminates only its own process group. Known resource
property and audio warnings are not automatically treated as shader failures.
There is also an advisory lock preventing two matrix runners at once. Process
inspection covers the project's dev launchers and common direct Minecraft Java
launchers; manually operated exotic launchers still require operator exclusion.

Each condition appears once in each repeat block. Williams rows balance order
positions and carryover over a complete design cycle; a partial 3–5-repeat cycle
is interleaved but is **not** claimed perfectly balanced. A two-condition,
four-repeat matrix gives AB/BA/AB/BA. Both runtime stacks can be interleaved in
one matrix instead of measuring the whole minimal stack before optimized.

## Commands

Start with a dry run (no writes, build or client launch):

```sh
python3 scripts/run_proof_matrix.py forest-high forest-patched-off forest-adaptive --profiles-root run-workloads/photon-proof --stacks minimal optimized --repeats 3 --dry-run
```

```sh
# Premium cloud scene plus simpler existing-quality control: 12 JVM runs.
```

startup/shutdown time: 18 runs take at least 22.5 minutes of warmup/capture and
usually substantially longer. Prefer completing one matrix before expanding the
set. `--skip-build` skips only the initial build. `--warmup`, `--duration`,
`--timeout`, `--sample-interval`, and `--no-gpu-queries` are explicit controls;
keep them matched within a comparison. CPU wall/thread clocks remain separate
from actual GPU measurements. CPU layer profiling is disabled by default in the
runner to reduce measurement overhead.

## Analysis and uncertainty

Each new tag produces `dev/logs/TAG/matrix-manifest.json`, console logs,
measurements, summaries and `matrix-analysis.json`. Existing tags are refused.
Failed matrices remain marked failed and are not silently ranked. Rerun with a
new tag after correcting the failure; preserve the failed evidence.
The initial `sustained-v2-main` matrix is retained as failed: its first baseline
hit the old raw-file guard after Iris normalized an otherwise equivalent option
file. This was a tooling mismatch, not a demonstrated shader-quality change.

The analysis reports the median, min/max and median absolute deviation across
**independent JVM runs** for FPS-derived frame duration, GPU mean/median/p95,
CPU wall/thread means and CPU wall p95. Candidate time reductions are paired
against the scene's original-high run in the same repeat block and runtime
stack. Positive percentages mean lower time. Runtime-stack comparisons are
separate from ShaderLOD's incremental comparisons. Geometry/detail changes and
simpler quality controls are annotated; upstream quality settings must match for
adaptive and patched-disabled comparisons.

Frame samples are autocorrelated. Thousands of frames are not thousands of
independent replicates. No IID confidence interval or significance claim is
produced. Three to five repeats remain exploratory; per-run p95 describes tail
latency and is not uncertainty on the speedup. Order drift, shared hardware
activity and thermal/cache state can still matter. Do not choose the best repeat
or drop an anomalous run because it weakens the result.

GPU scope boundaries, coarse Apple elapsed-query attribution, CPU/driver time
and overlapping scopes retain the limits in [GPU_TIMING.md](GPU_TIMING.md).
Correct timings do not prove visual quality: inspect transitions, motion and
salient lighting separately.

# Benchmark guide

For the local Asahi machine without a desktop, see [headless development](HEADLESS.md).
The maintained Linux ARM64 launcher selects its installed GPU-backed virtual
display when no display is explicitly selected; the native 2560×1600 viewport
and all normal benchmark guards remain required.

For the prepared RTX 2080 Ti Windows host, see [Windows benchmarking](WINDOWS_BENCHMARK.md).

Use the maintained command for discovery, planning, execution and results:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py discover
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py baseline --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --output FRESH_BASELINE
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py plan --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py check --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_CHECK_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py report --output REPORT
```

`discover` lists local managed slots, worlds and shader archives. It is an inventory, not compatibility approval. Use `--profile` instead of `--slot` for an explicit prepared client. Set `--width` and `--height` to the intended native viewport (the local Asahi fullscreen mode is 2560×1600). Select the exact original pack/options for the feature; private candidates use `--candidate` instead of `--feature`. See the [candidate reference](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md) for specialized scenes, compatibility checks and qualification protocols.

`baseline` renders the original pack with the main mod absent in the backed-up
authored save. After 120 seconds conditioning it captures three unchanged
20-second native windows, with the standard ownership, readiness, sample and
restoration checks. The report gives frame sample variance/SD (ms²/ms), and
separately variance/SD of the three window means and first-to-last drift.
These describe frame jitter and within-process variation, respectively; neither
is a confidence interval. Repeat in fresh processes to measure between-run
variation. Keep absent-mod baselines separate from the matched Master-Off
controls in optimization comparisons. Startup failure supplies no frame-time
measurement. `native-startup` remains a short original-only startup diagnostic.

`--gl-context native` preserves Minecraft's normal context request. For explicit
desktop API coverage, maintained comparisons also accept `3.2`, `4.3`, `4.5` and
`4.6`. These request real GLFW contexts; they do not override reported versions
or capabilities. Explicit requests disable NeoForge's reusable early window in
the owned profile, with the normal configuration backup/CAS/restoration contract.
The returned desktop version must meet the requested minimum and is recorded in
`summary.json.gl_context`. A driver returning4.6 for a4.5 request is labeled4.6;
it does not supply an independent4.5 result. Keep actual context/configuration
cohorts and their native baselines separate. Frozen Bliss qualification retains
its existing native-context protocol and refuses an explicit context override.
`--expected-renderer 'RTX 5080'` additionally refuses a ready client on a different
GPU, including a hardware integrated GPU. It validates the observed renderer
before scoring; it does not select the GPU or change personal driver settings.

`--performance-stack optimized` selects the exact pinned ModernFix, FerriteCore
and ImmediatelyFast tuple for G03 and its matched original-only startup/baselines.
Default remains `minimal`. Other private/frozen protocols reject this override.
Preflight verifies every optional JAR, launch uses the maintained stack selector,
and runtime readiness checks the actual loaded module versions before scoring.
Optional artifacts are frozen operation inputs. Keep stack cohorts separate;
selecting the tuple is not proof that G03 compiled, executed, or helped.

`plan` runs the standard test's static checks without compiling, launching or creating the report. It lists the resolved launch plan, schedule, per-check elapsed time, failures and remedies. A stale build is reported; `test` rebuilds it automatically before launch. Native options and canonical profile inputs are checked; preserve unexplained differences before resetting a managed slot. Runtime-only checks still run in the client.

`check` accepts the same candidate arguments and exercises activation, available source/work checks, short captures and restoration without the two-minute conditioning period. It reports no performance or visual qualification. Use it when checking whether a newly integrated candidate runs; use `test` for a development performance comparison. Frozen Bliss qualification cannot use `check`.

`test` uses the fixed native/candidate/native-return protocol described below. `report` reads existing reports without launching anything, including historical reports. Its decision gives drift comparison precedence over an averaged positive mean, and identifies invalid runs or recovery requirements. It does not grant optimization closure or compatibility qualification. Phase timings in `summary.json` include nested profile preparation/restoration details; do not sum nested details into the total again.

For optimization iteration use the maintained standard test, on the authorized machine with a prepared managed client slot and authentic original pack and options:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test \
  --profile /path/to/prepared/client \
  --pack /path/to/original-pack.zip \
  --pack-options /path/to/original-pack.zip.txt \
  --feature PUBLIC_OPTIMIZATION_ID \
  --output /path/to/fresh/report
```

The command automatically selects the existing Linux ARM64 launcher on that platform. Explicit `linux_arm64_runtime.py` commands remain supported. It finds an installed full JDK21 or a cached Gradle JDK21; an explicit JAVA_HOME retains precedence. Select an existing loader/version/scene slot; keep the report outside that slot and on the same filesystem as the profile. Confirm the lane is free and the inputs match the intended tuple before launch. Do not reset a slot owned by a client or interrupted operation. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py checkout --help` describes managed checkout. Use `run_storage.copytree` for profile/world copies; it enforces storage limits.

The standard test targets the prepared NeoForge 1.21.1 benchmark protocol. It renders native Off for 120 seconds before measurement, then acquires native Off, singleton candidate through normal Apply, then native Off return: 20 seconds each, with separate warmup, startup and recovery within a 900-second budget. Conditioning was added after repeated first-to-return drift; it does not prove stability. It records total-frame timing, drift, stills and restoration in the report. A valid slower result is still a result; a failed or invalid run is not a speed conclusion. Inspect `summary.json`, errors and restoration before proceeding. A short result is not proof of visual equivalence, DH/PBR compatibility or final closure. Compare matched total-frame measurements and disclose drift and scope.

C02 is an explicitly labeled 2×2 bloom quality tradeoff, with Master-On native
controls; its scoped exception is documented in the [candidate reference](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md#c02-experimental-bloom-shading-rate).

## Choose the check for the question

| Question | Maintained route | What it does not establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What inputs and candidates exist? | `discover`, then `plan` with selected inputs | Runtime compatibility or ownership |
| Does this change activate and recover? | `check` | Performance or visual equivalence |
| Is the idea worth more investigation? | `test`, then `report` | Broad workload/machine qualification |
| What does native do without ShaderLOD? | `baseline` | Installed-Off overhead by itself |
| Does it preserve motion or work across packs/hardware? | Candidate-specific protocols in the reference | Coverage of untested scenes, transitions or machines |

Before designing a new study, establish the user's intended decision: deep
workload performance, compatibility breadth, quality, or a quick screen. Reuse
the supported commands above. Put the chosen claim, comparator, coverage, useful
metrics, controls and budget in the existing experiment record. Record exclusions
and fallback separately; do not impose a universal repetition count or payback
horizon. Performance requires actual-window execution and valid output evidence,
not merely enabling a setting. Source changes do not inherit earlier timings.

## B17: a distinct conditional premise, not a cone implementation

A full hierarchy is not the only new cost premise. A **certified current
per-sprite upper height bound** can establish an initial empty ray interval.
The table's 31/31/53 index-depth intervals are an idealized opportunity before
filter/rounding margins and native boundary semantics; they are not saved
fetch counts or a speed estimate. This could avoid actual height reads while
keeping the native sample count and later hit/lighting algorithm.

The missing certificate must join exact resource priority and PNG contents to
the current atlas texture, sprite coordinates, gutter/mip construction, sampler
filter/anisotropy, animation/interpolation frame and resource-reload generation.
It must bound every positive-weight filter contributor and account for numeric
rounding. A block/material group is not a sprite identity: the existing eligible
Complementary groups include other stones, machinery and wood faces. Unknown,
cutout, animated, replacement/CTM, DH/VOXY and unsupported PBR inputs remain native.
The inspected resource's metadata contains animation elsewhere; selected static
filenames do not certify the whole resource pack or a future reload.

Even with that certificate, reproduce the precise first-sample/prestep/dither,
loop condition, return UV/depth and preceding self-shadow position. Complementary
computes coordinates from index×interval; Photon/BSL/Solas/AstraLex repeatedly
add steps. A multiply jump is not an exact replacement on the latter paths.
Retaining their additions while omitting certified reads may be an exact route,
but its ALU/branch cost and driver treatment are unmeasured. Complementary's
`inout texDepth` also arrives from an uninitialized caller local in the inspected
source: preserve actual entry/prestep semantics, never assume a new initial
value and call it equivalent. No candidate attempts to repair upstream behavior.

General cone/min/max traversal remains a larger separate option. The primary
[relaxed cone stepping description](https://developer.nvidia.com/gpugems/gpugems3/part-iii-rendering/chapter-18-relaxed-cone-stepping-relief-mapping)
uses precomputed cone data and refinement. Continuous surface accuracy does not
guarantee the same sampled native first hit. A local implementation would need
all atlas boundaries, animated-frame updates, conservative storage/filtering,
light-ray uses and fallback rules, plus an explicit added-sampler plan. Ordinary
normal-alpha mipmaps are not a certified maximum hierarchy.

Count preprocessing/upload/update amortization, metadata reads, traversal ALU,
native-equivalent policy overhead and lost specialization against actual active
native height reads. The native counts here span 40/64/128 with early exits and
fades; none is an executed-cost measurement. No hierarchy build or cone builder
is warranted before the cheap certificate/coverage gate.
